```rust
/// Digest of a warrant's signed claims — the `token_digest` on its delegation link.
pub(crate) fn warrant_claims_digest(warrant: &Warrant) -> String {
    match serde_json::to_value(&warrant.claims) {
        Ok(value) => match serde_json::to_string(&canonicalize(&value)) {
            Ok(text) => format!("sha256:{}", sha256_hex(text.as_bytes())),
            Err(_) => "sha256:unavailable".to_string(),
        },
        Err(_) => "sha256:unavailable".to_string(),
    }
}

fn claims_digest(stored: &StoredWarrant) -> String {
    warrant_claims_digest(&stored.warrant)
}

/// The one-link authority block for a warrant, built the same way for the report receipt and
/// for every per-effect receipt so the two cannot drift (the module doc's second hazard).
pub(crate) fn warrant_authority(warrant: &Warrant) -> evidence::Authority {
    let claims = &warrant.claims;
    let chain = vec![evidence::DelegationLink {
        issuer: warrant.issuer_key.clone(),
        subject: claims.subject.clone(),
        capabilities: claims.bounds.tools.iter().cloned().collect(),
        not_before: claims.issued_at,
        not_after: claims.bounds.expires_at,
        token_digest: warrant_claims_digest(warrant),
    }];
    evidence::Authority {
        effective_capabilities: evidence::recompute_intersection(&chain),
        intersection_proof: evidence::compute_intersection_proof(&chain),
        chain,
    }
}

/// Digest of the bounds a warrant is evaluated against — its "policy".
pub(crate) fn bounds_policy_digest(bounds: &WarrantBounds) -> String {
    match serde_json::to_value(bounds) {
        Ok(value) => match serde_json::to_string(&canonicalize(&value)) {
            Ok(text) => format!("sha256:{}", sha256_hex(text.as_bytes())),
            Err(_) => "sha256:unavailable".to_string(),
        },
        Err(_) => "sha256:unavailable".to_string(),
    }
}
```

```rust
/// [`SignedReport::effect_receipts`]; these ids are what the digest covers.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct EffectReceiptLine {

    /// The tool that performed it.

    /// `binding.receipt_id` of the pre-commit receipt.

/// The per-effect evidence section: which effects were performed under which receipts.

/// about every report exported before this section existed. Absent is never "nothing was
/// performed".
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct EffectEvidenceSection {

    pub receipts_consulted: usize,
    /// One line per pre-commit, in issuance order.
    pub effects: Vec<EffectReceiptLine>,

     staged effects were performed under a pre-commit receipt. That is not a statement that none \
```

```rust
    /// Attach the receipt log: the bundle lists every chain, the export carries the receipts.
    ///
    /// Replaces [`NO_EFFECT_RECEIPTS_LIMITATION`] with what was actually read. A log that verifies
    /// nothing is still recorded — an empty section is "consulted, and empty", which differs from
    /// `None`.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn with_effect_receipts(mut self, receipts: Vec<evidence::WarReceipt>) -> Self {
        let effects = crate::receipts::chains(&receipts)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|chain| EffectReceiptLine {
                handle: chain.pre_commit.predicate.operation.target.clone(),
                tool: chain.pre_commit.predicate.operation.class.clone(),
                pre_receipt_id: chain.pre_commit.predicate.binding.receipt_id.clone(),
                post_receipt_id: chain.post_commit.as_ref().map(|p| p.predicate.binding.receipt_id.clone()),
                status: chain
                    .post_commit
                    .as_ref()
                    .and_then(|p| p.predicate.outcome.as_ref().map(|o| o.status.clone()))
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "unfinished".to_string()),
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        self.bundle.limitations.retain(|l| l != NO_EFFECT_RECEIPTS_LIMITATION);
        self.bundle.limitations.push(format!(
            "{} per-effect receipt chain(s) are attached, each advisory: the pre-commit was signed \
             before settle performed the effect and the post-commit after, which records what \
             settle did, not that the agent held no other way to do the same thing in the world.",
            effects.len()
        ));
        self.bundle.effect_evidence = Some(EffectEvidenceSection {
            receipts_consulted: receipts.len(),
            effects,
        });
        self.effect_receipts = receipts;
        self
    }
```

```rust
#[test]
fn a_pre_commit_receipt_is_on_disk_before_the_effect_is_performed() {
    let dir = tempdir("before");
    let mut warrant = warrant_with_tools(&["github.create_pr", "github.comment"]);
    let queue = queue_with_pr_and_comment(&dir);
    let log_path = dir.join("receipts.jsonl");
    let mut log = ReceiptLog::open(&log_path).expect("log");
    let mut inner = Counting { log_path: log_path.clone(), fail_at: None, performed: Vec::new(), lines_on_disk_when_performing: Vec::new() };
    let witness = witness(&warrant);
    let mut performer = EvidencedPerformer::new(&mut inner, witness, &mut log);

    let report = settle(&mut warrant, &queue, None, &settle_key().verifying_key(), &mut performer)
        .expect("settle");
    drop(performer);

    assert!(report.complete);
    // Effect 1 saw 1 line (its own pre-commit); effect 2 saw 3 (pre, post, pre).
    assert_eq!(inner.lines_on_disk_when_performing, vec![1, 3]);
    assert_eq!(warrant.state, WarrantState::Settled);
}

#[test]
fn every_released_effect_has_a_chain_that_verifies_and_names_its_real_id() {
    let dir = tempdir("chain");
    let mut warrant = warrant_with_tools(&["github.create_pr", "github.comment"]);
    let queue = queue_with_pr_and_comment(&dir);
    let mut log = ReceiptLog::open(dir.join("receipts.jsonl")).expect("log");
    let mut inner = Counting { log_path: dir.join("receipts.jsonl"), fail_at: None, performed: Vec::new(), lines_on_disk_when_performing: Vec::new() };
    let witness = witness(&warrant);
    let mut performer = EvidencedPerformer::new(&mut inner, witness, &mut log);
    settle(&mut warrant, &queue, None, &settle_key().verifying_key(), &mut performer).expect("settle");
    assert!(performer.unrecorded().is_empty());
    drop(performer);

    let chains = chains(log.receipts());
    assert_eq!(log.len(), 4);
    assert_eq!(chains.len(), 2);
    for (chain, expected_real_id) in chains.iter().zip(["real-1", "real-2"]) {
        let post = chain.post_commit.as_ref().expect("post-commit");
        evidence::verify_chain(&chain.pre_commit, post).expect("chain verifies");
        let outcome = post.predicate.outcome.as_ref().expect("outcome");
        assert_eq!(outcome.status, "success");
        assert_eq!(outcome.effects, vec![expected_real_id.to_string()]);
        assert_eq!(chain.pre_commit.predicate.binding.enforcement_mode, evidence::EnforcementMode::Advisory);
        assert_eq!(chain.pre_commit.predicate.operation.method, "settle");
        assert!(!chain.pre_commit.predicate.operation.reversible);
    }
    assert_eq!(chains[0].pre_commit.predicate.operation.target, format!("pr://staged/{ID}/1"));
}

/// The refusal Rule 2 requires before any label moves: an effect for a tool the warrant does not
/// hold is refused at the authority gate, before `perform`, and no receipt is written for it.
#[test]
fn an_effect_for_a_tool_the_warrant_does_not_hold_is_refused_before_it_is_performed() {
    let dir = tempdir("deny");
    let mut warrant = warrant_with_tools(&["github.create_pr"]);
    let queue = queue_with_pr_and_comment(&dir);
    let mut log = ReceiptLog::open(dir.join("receipts.jsonl")).expect("log");
    let mut inner = Counting { log_path: dir.join("receipts.jsonl"), fail_at: None, performed: Vec::new(), lines_on_disk_when_performing: Vec::new() };
    let witness = witness(&warrant);
    let mut performer = EvidencedPerformer::new(&mut inner, witness, &mut log);
    let report = settle(&mut warrant, &queue, None, &settle_key().verifying_key(), &mut performer).expect("settle");
    drop(performer);

    assert!(!report.complete);
    assert_eq!(inner.performed, vec![format!("pr://staged/{ID}/1")]);
    match &report.effects[1] {
        EffectOutcome::Failed { handle, reason } => {
            assert_eq!(handle, &format!("comment://staged/{ID}/2"));
            assert_eq!(reason, "refused by the notary at the authority gate; nothing was performed");
            assert!(!reason.contains("github.comment"), "Deny carries only the gate: {reason}");
        }
        other => panic!("expected the comment to be refused, got {other:?}"),
    }
    assert_eq!(log.len(), 2, "a refused effect gets no receipt; the PR got pre and post");
    assert_eq!(warrant.state, WarrantState::Held);
}

    assert_eq!(outcome.status, "failed");
    assert_eq!(outcome.error.as_deref(), Some("upstream returned 503"));
```

```rust
    let queue = queue_with_pr_and_comment(dir);
    let mut log = ReceiptLog::open(dir.join("receipts.jsonl")).expect("log");
    let mut inner = Counting { log_path: dir.join("receipts.jsonl"), fail_at: None, performed: Vec::new(), lines_on_disk_when_performing: Vec::new() };
    let witness = witness(&warrant);
    let mut performer = EvidencedPerformer::new(&mut inner, witness, &mut log);
    settle(&mut warrant, &queue, None, &settle_key().verifying_key(), &mut performer).expect("settle");
    drop(performer);
    build(&stored_from(&warrant), Ok(&queue), &issuer().verifying_key(), NOW + 60)
        .with_effect_receipts(log.receipts().to_vec())
        .sign(&issuer(), "issuer")
        .expect("sign")
}

#[test]
fn the_export_embeds_the_chain_and_verifies_offline() {
    let dir = tempdir("export");
    let signed = settled_export(&dir);
    let section = signed.bundle.effect_evidence.as_ref().expect("section");
    assert_eq!(section.receipts_consulted, 4);
    assert_eq!(section.effects.len(), 2);
    assert!(section.effects.iter().all(|line| line.status == "success"));
    assert_eq!(signed.effect_receipts.len(), 4);
    verify_export(&signed).expect("verifies");
    verify_export_signed_by(&signed, &issuer().verifying_key()).expect("verifies against the pin");
    let json = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&signed).expect("encode");
    let back: warrantor_warrant::report::SignedReport = serde_json::from_slice(&json).expect("decode");
    verify_export(&back).expect("round trip verifies");
}

#[test]
fn removing_one_receipt_from_the_export_is_a_commit_gate_violation() {
    let dir = tempdir("removed");
    let signed = settled_export(&dir);

    let mut without_post = signed.clone();
    without_post.effect_receipts.remove(3);
    let err = verify_export(&without_post).unwrap_err().to_string();
    assert!(err.contains("commit-gate violation (I-07)"), "{err}");

    let mut without_pre = signed.clone();
    without_pre.effect_receipts.remove(0);
    let err = verify_export(&without_pre).unwrap_err().to_string();
    assert!(err.contains("commit-gate violation (I-07)"), "{err}");
}

#[test]
fn a_chain_signed_by_another_key_cannot_ride_along() {
    let dir = tempdir("foreign");
    let mut signed = settled_export(&dir);
    let stranger = SigningKey::from_bytes(&[5; 32]);
    let pre = evidence::issue_pre_commit(signed.effect_receipts[0].predicate.clone(), &stranger, "stranger");
    let post = evidence::issue_post_commit(
        &pre,
        signed.effect_receipts[1].predicate.outcome.clone().expect("outcome"),
        &stranger,
        "stranger",
    );
    signed.effect_receipts[0] = pre;
    signed.effect_receipts[1] = post;
    assert!(matches!(verify_export(&signed), Err(ReportError::Binding(_))));
}

#[test]
fn a_bundle_that_lists_a_status_its_receipt_does_not_carry_is_refused() {
    let dir = tempdir("status");
    let signed = settled_export(&dir);
    let mut tampered = signed.clone();
    let post = &mut tampered.effect_receipts[1];
    post.predicate.outcome.as_mut().expect("outcome").status = "failed".to_string();
    // Changing the predicate breaks its signature first; that is the right first failure.
    assert!(matches!(verify_export(&tampered), Err(ReportError::Evidence(_))));
}

#[test]
fn an_export_built_without_a_receipt_log_still_verifies_and_says_so() {
    let dir = tempdir("older");
    let warrant = warrant_with_tools(&["github.create_pr"]);
    let queue = StagingQueue::open(dir.join("q.jsonl"), ID, EffectRegistry::github()).expect("q");
    let signed = build(&stored_from(&warrant), Ok(&queue), &issuer().verifying_key(), NOW)
        .sign(&issuer(), "issuer")
        .expect("sign");
    assert!(signed.bundle.effect_evidence.is_none());
    assert!(signed.effect_receipts.is_empty());
    let canonical = warrantor_warrant::report::canonical_bundle(&signed.bundle).expect("canonical");
    assert!(!canonical.contains("effect_evidence"), "absent must stay absent: {canonical}");
    assert!(signed.bundle.limitations.iter().any(|l| l == warrantor_warrant::report::NO_EFFECT_RECEIPTS_LIMITATION));
    verify_export(&signed).expect("verifies");
}

#[test]
fn stray_receipts_the_bundle_does_not_list_are_refused() {
    let dir = tempdir("stray");
    let mut signed = settled_export(&dir);
    let extra = signed.effect_receipts[0].clone();
    signed.effect_receipts.push(extra);
    assert!(matches!(verify_export(&signed), Err(ReportError::Binding(_))));
}
```

- [ ] **Step 7 — Implement `verify_effect_receipts`**

In report.rs, before `Ok(())` at the end of `verify_export` (line 1115), add `verify_effect_receipts(export)?;` and the function after `verify_export`:

```rust
/// Every chain the bundle lists must be present, verify as a pre→post pair (I-07, I-02), be
/// signed by the report's own key, and describe the handle and status the bundle says it does.
fn verify_effect_receipts(export: &SignedReport) -> Result<(), ReportError> {
    let signer = &export.evidence_receipt.signature.public_key;
    let find = |id: &str| {
        export
            .effect_receipts
            .iter()
            .find(|r| r.predicate.binding.receipt_id == id)
    };
    let missing = |what: &str, handle: &str| {
        ReportError::Evidence(
            evidence::EvidenceError::CommitGate(format!(
                "the {what} receipt for {handle} is missing from the export"
            ))
            .to_string(),
        )
    };
    let Some(section) = &export.bundle.effect_evidence else {
        if export.effect_receipts.is_empty() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        return Err(ReportError::Binding(
            "the export carries effect receipts the bundle does not list".to_string(),
        ));
    };
    let mut expected = 0usize;
    for line in &section.effects {
        expected += 1;
        let pre = find(&line.pre_receipt_id).ok_or_else(|| missing("pre-commit", &line.handle))?;
        if pre.signature.public_key != *signer {
            return Err(ReportError::Binding(format!(
                "the pre-commit receipt for {} was signed by a key other than the report's",
                line.handle
            )));
        }
        if pre.predicate.operation.target != line.handle || pre.predicate.operation.class != line.tool {
            return Err(ReportError::Binding(format!(
                "the pre-commit receipt listed for {} is over a different effect",
                line.handle
            )));
        }
        if pre.predicate.actor.principal != export.bundle.subject {
            return Err(ReportError::Binding(format!(
                "the pre-commit receipt for {} names a different subject",
                line.handle
            )));
        }
        let Some(post_id) = &line.post_receipt_id else {
            evidence::verify_receipt(pre).map_err(|e| ReportError::Evidence(e.to_string()))?;
            evidence::verify_authority(&pre.predicate.authority)
                .map_err(|e| ReportError::Evidence(e.to_string()))?;
            if line.status != "unfinished" {
                return Err(ReportError::Binding(format!(
                    "{} has no post-commit receipt but the bundle records status {:?}",
                    line.handle, line.status
                )));
            }
            continue;
        };
        expected += 1;
        let post = find(post_id).ok_or_else(|| missing("post-commit", &line.handle))?;
        evidence::verify_chain(pre, post).map_err(|e| ReportError::Evidence(e.to_string()))?;
        if post.signature.public_key != *signer {
            return Err(ReportError::Binding(format!(
                "the post-commit receipt for {} was signed by a key other than the report's",
                line.handle
            )));
        }
        let status = post
            .predicate
            .outcome
            .as_ref()
            .map(|o| o.status.as_str())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        if status != line.status {
            return Err(ReportError::Binding(format!(
                "the bundle records {} as {:?}; its post-commit receipt says {status:?}",
                line.handle, line.status
            )));
        }
    }
    if export.effect_receipts.len() != expected {
        return Err(ReportError::Binding(format!(
            "the export carries {} effect receipt(s) and the bundle lists {expected}; receipts \
             the bundle does not account for are refused",
            export.effect_receipts.len()
        )));
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

Note the ordering inside `verify_export`: digest, both report receipts, same-key, modes, bindings, **then** chains — so a tampered bundle still reads as tampered before a missing receipt reads as I-07. Run: `cargo test -p warrantor-warrant --test report_evidence_chain -j 2` → 11 passed. ### 2.5 Evidence and notary reach the settle path — **wired 2026-09-<dd>, one adapter, advisory**

```markdown
The log sits on the same disk as the agent's worktree; L7-02's external recorder is the archive
push, which files the export and not the log. MCP `settle_warrant` still uses `NoAdapter` and
performs nothing, so it issues nothing. `warrantor stage` still does not check the tool allowlist;
the notary's authority gate now refuses such an effect at settle, which is the first refusal in
this path and the reason the label is what it is (Rule 2).
```

### Task 1.2: The egress broker into the `--egress` flag, with capability-derived destinations (L4-02, L4-23)

Anchor (plan-brief.md, L4-23): "The agent never sees a URL parameter. It selects a governed capability ... There is no field into which a raw host, IP address or link can be written, so an invented destination is not denied; it is unexpressible" — and L4-02's incident fact: "Agents obtained internet access by exploiting a separate, previously unknown Artifactory vulnerability to move beyond their intended environment S01 §IV.A".

**What the survey got wrong, and what this task therefore is.** `warrantor_egress` is *not* orphaned: `rust/warrant/src/egress.rs` already derives a `DestinationCatalog` from `WarrantBounds::egress_hosts` and `proxy::Proxy::decide` already calls `EgressBroker::decide` per destination. What is missing is the L4-23 half — the agent still supplies a raw host in `url`/`endpoint`/… arguments and the proxy filters it — and the receipt half: an allow leaves no record at all, and a deny is recorded only as a `RefusalRecord` at session end, outside any signed bundle. This task (a) makes destinations catalog capability names in enforce mode, with `--egress H,H` compiled into the same catalog, (b) records every egress decision durably *before* the call is forwarded, and (c) has `warrantor report` sign those decisions into `EgressReceipt`s inside the bundle, verified by `warrantor verify`. `bound_strengths()` is not touched: `egress_hosts` stays `Mediated`, and the bundle keeps saying so.

**Files:**
- Create `rust/warrant/src/catalog.rs` — format `warrantor.destination-catalog/1`, sign/verify, the agent-visible vocabulary.
- Modify `rust/warrant/src/lib.rs` (lines 35–70: `pub mod` list) — add `pub mod catalog;`.
- Modify `rust/warrant/src/egress.rs` (lines 262–376 `Destination`/`DESTINATION_KEYS`/`destinations_of`; append after line 499) — make `DESTINATION_KEYS` public, add `EgressDecision`, the decision log.
- Modify `rust/warrant/src/proxy.rs` (lines 111–121 `Proxy` fields; 170–228 `decide`; 279–284 `egress_broker`) — vocabulary resolution, allow-decision capture.
- Modify `rust/warrant/src/mcp_endpoints.rs` (lines 656–716 `AgentEndpoint` fields/`new`; 947–1004 `tools`; 1006–1183 `call`) — catalog builder, schema constraint, log-before-forward.
- Modify `rust/egress/src/lib.rs` (lines 275–290 `EgressReceiptBody`/`EgressReceipt`) — add `Eq` so the receipt can live inside `ReportBundle` (which derives `Eq`).

```rust
//! The destination catalog: the vocabulary an agent selects destinations from (L4-23).
//!
//! The agent never writes a host. A tool argument that names a destination carries a capability
//! NAME; the proxy resolves the name through this catalog to the host the signed warrant bounds.
//! `--egress H,H` is sugar: each host becomes the capability `host:<H>`, so the old flag and the
//! new one produce the same object and the proxy has one path, not two.
//!
//! The per-warrant catalog is signed by the issuer at grant time and verified against the
//! on-disk issuer key at `mcp` time. It cannot widen the warrant: `vocabulary_within` refuses any
//! capability whose host is outside `WarrantBounds::egress_hosts`. Enforcement is unchanged by any
//! of this — it is the MCP proxy, and only the MCP proxy. See [`crate::egress::ENFORCEMENT_NOTE`].

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::net::IpAddr;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use ed25519_dalek::{Signature, Signer, SigningKey, Verifier, VerifyingKey};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::{json, Value};
use warrantor_egress::DenyReason;

use crate::egress::DESTINATION_KEYS;
use crate::report::sha256_hex;
use crate::WarrantBounds;

/// Wire format. A new shape gets a new name, never a silent change.
pub const CATALOG_FORMAT: &str = "warrantor.destination-catalog/1";
const SIGNING_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"warrantor.destination-catalog/1\n";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Capability {
    pub name: String,
    pub host: String,
    pub purpose: String,
    pub permitted_methods: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CatalogSignature {
    pub key_id: String,
    pub public_key: String,
    pub value: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct CapabilityCatalog {
    pub format: String,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub warrant_id: Option<String>,
    pub capabilities: Vec<Capability>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub signature: Option<CatalogSignature>,
}

/// A name is a name: no scheme, no slash, no IP literal, 1..=64 chars of `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`.
pub fn check_capability_name(name: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    if name.is_empty() || name.len() > 64 {
        return Err(format!("capability name {name:?} must be 1 to 64 characters"));
    }
    if name.contains("://") || name.contains('/') || name.parse::<IpAddr>().is_ok() {
        return Err(format!(
            "capability name {name:?} looks like an address; a capability is a name the \
             catalog resolves, never a place"
        ));
    }
    if !name
        .chars()
        .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '.' | '_' | ':' | '-'))
    {
        return Err(format!("capability name {name:?} has characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._:-]"));
    }
    Ok(())
}

impl CapabilityCatalog {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn from_hosts(hosts: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            format: CATALOG_FORMAT.to_string(),
            warrant_id: None,
            capabilities: hosts
                .iter()
                .map(|host| Capability {
                    name: format!("host:{host}"),
                    host: host.clone(),
                    purpose: format!("--egress {host} (compiled from the flag)"),
                    permitted_methods: Vec::new(),
                })
                .collect(),
            signature: None,
        }
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn for_warrant(warrant_id: &str, capabilities: Vec<Capability>) -> Self {
        Self {
            format: CATALOG_FORMAT.to_string(),
            warrant_id: Some(warrant_id.to_string()),
            capabilities,
            signature: None,
        }
    }

    /// The named capabilities, or the first name this catalog does not hold.
    pub fn select(&self, names: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Result<Vec<Capability>, String> {
        names
            .iter()
            .map(|name| {
                self.capabilities
                    .iter()
                    .find(|c| &c.name == name)
                    .cloned()
                    .ok_or_else(|| format!("{name} is not a capability in this catalog"))
            })
            .collect()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn hosts(&self) -> BTreeSet<String> {
        self.capabilities.iter().map(|c| c.host.clone()).collect()
    }

    fn signable(&self) -> Result<String, String> {
        let body = json!({
            "format": self.format,
            "warrant_id": self.warrant_id,
            "capabilities": self.capabilities,
        });
        serde_json::to_string(&crate::report::canonicalize(&body))
            .map_err(|e| format!("encode catalog: {e}"))
    }

    /// SHA-256 over the canonical signable body: what a receipt names.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn digest(&self) -> String {
        sha256_hex(self.signable().unwrap_or_default().as_bytes())
    }
}
```

```rust
fn signed_catalog(warrant_id: &str, issuer: &SigningKey) -> CapabilityCatalog {
    let hosts: BTreeSet<String> = ["api.github.com".to_string()].into_iter().collect();
    let mut catalog =
        CapabilityCatalog::for_warrant(warrant_id, CapabilityCatalog::from_hosts(&hosts).capabilities);

#[test]
fn a_signed_catalog_round_trips_through_disk_and_verifies_against_the_issuer() {
    let issuer = SigningKey::from_bytes(&[1; 32]);
    let dir = tempdir("roundtrip");
    let catalog = signed_catalog("wrt_1", &issuer);
    let path = warrantor_warrant::catalog::catalog_path(&dir, "wrt_1");
    catalog.save(&path).expect("save");
    let loaded = CapabilityCatalog::load(&path).expect("load");
    assert_eq!(loaded, catalog);
    loaded.verify(&issuer.verifying_key(), "wrt_1").expect("verifies");
    let stranger = SigningKey::from_bytes(&[9; 32]);
    assert!(loaded.verify(&stranger.verifying_key(), "wrt_1").is_err());
    assert!(loaded.verify(&issuer.verifying_key(), "wrt_2").is_err(), "bound to one warrant");
    let mut tampered = loaded.clone();
    tampered.capabilities[0].host = "evil.example".to_string();
    assert!(tampered.verify(&issuer.verifying_key(), "wrt_1").is_err());
}

fn a_catalog_cannot_name_a_host_outside_the_signed_bound() {
    let issuer = SigningKey::from_bytes(&[1; 32]);
    let mut catalog = signed_catalog("wrt_1", &issuer);
    catalog.capabilities.push(Capability {
        name: "exfil".to_string(),
        host: "paste.example".to_string(),
        purpose: "not in the bound".to_string(),
        permitted_methods: Vec::new(),
    });
    let err = catalog
        .vocabulary_within(&bounds_with(&["api.github.com"]))
        .expect_err("widening refused");
    assert!(err.contains("paste.example"), "{err}");
    let vocabulary = signed_catalog("wrt_1", &issuer)
        .vocabulary_within(&bounds_with(&["api.github.com"]))
        .expect("within");
    assert_eq!(vocabulary.names(), vec!["host:api.github.com".to_string()]);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 4 — Sign, verify, load, save, vocabulary.** Append to `catalog.rs` inside `impl CapabilityCatalog`:

```rust
    pub fn sign(&mut self, key: &SigningKey, key_id: &str) {
        let mut message = SIGNING_DOMAIN.to_vec();
        message.extend_from_slice(self.signable().unwrap_or_default().as_bytes());
        let sig: Signature = key.sign(&message);
        self.signature = Some(CatalogSignature {
            key_id: key_id.to_string(),
            public_key: hex::encode(key.verifying_key().to_bytes()),
            value: hex::encode(sig.to_bytes()),
        });
    }

    /// Verify against a key pinned out of band, and that the catalog names `warrant_id`.
    pub fn verify(&self, issuer: &VerifyingKey, warrant_id: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        if self.format != CATALOG_FORMAT {
            return Err(format!("{:?} is not {CATALOG_FORMAT}", self.format));
        }
        if self.warrant_id.as_deref() != Some(warrant_id) {
            return Err(format!(
                "catalog names warrant {:?}, not {warrant_id}",
                self.warrant_id
            ));
        }
        let Some(signature) = &self.signature else {
            return Err("the catalog is unsigned; an unsigned catalog verifies nothing".to_string());
        };
        if signature.public_key != hex::encode(issuer.to_bytes()) {
            return Err("the catalog was signed by a key that is not the pinned issuer".to_string());
        }
        let raw = hex::decode(&signature.value).map_err(|e| format!("signature hex: {e}"))?;
        let bytes: [u8; 64] = raw
            .try_into()
            .map_err(|_| "signature must be 64 bytes".to_string())?;
        let mut message = SIGNING_DOMAIN.to_vec();
        message.extend_from_slice(self.signable()?.as_bytes());
        issuer
            .verify(&message, &Signature::from_bytes(&bytes))
            .map_err(|_| "catalog signature does not verify".to_string())
    }

    pub fn load(path: &Path) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let body = std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| format!("read {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        let declared: Value =
            serde_json::from_slice(&body).map_err(|e| format!("{} is not JSON: {e}", path.display()))?;
        match declared.get("format").and_then(Value::as_str) {
            Some(f) if f == CATALOG_FORMAT => {}
            other => {
                return Err(format!(
                    "{} declares format {other:?}; this build reads {CATALOG_FORMAT}",
                    path.display()
                ))
            }
        }
        serde_json::from_value(declared).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))
    }

    pub fn save(&self, path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
        if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| format!("create {}: {e}", parent.display()))?;
        }
        let text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(self).map_err(|e| format!("encode catalog: {e}"))?;
        std::fs::write(path, text).map_err(|e| format!("write {}: {e}", path.display()))
    }

    /// The names this warrant may use. Refuses a catalog that reaches past the signed bound.
    pub fn vocabulary_within(&self, bounds: &WarrantBounds) -> Result<Vocabulary, String> {
        let mut names = BTreeMap::new();
        for capability in &self.capabilities {
            check_capability_name(&capability.name)?;
            if !bounds.egress_hosts.contains(&capability.host) {
                return Err(format!(
                    "capability {} resolves to {}, which the warrant's egress bound does not \
                     name; a catalog file cannot widen a signed bound",
                    capability.name, capability.host
                ));
            }
            names.insert(capability.name.clone(), capability.host.clone());
        }
        Ok(Vocabulary { names, digest: self.digest() })
    }
}

#[must_use]
pub fn catalog_path(root: &Path, warrant_id: &str) -> PathBuf {
    root.join("catalogs").join(format!("{warrant_id}.json"))
}

/// Name → host, for the names this warrant may reach. Nothing else is expressible.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Vocabulary {
    names: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    digest: String,
}

impl Vocabulary {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn names(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        self.names.keys().cloned().collect()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn digest(&self) -> &str {
        &self.digest
    }

    /// `<name>` or `<name>/<path>` → `https://<host>/<path>`. Anything address-shaped is
    /// `NotACapability`; a name-shaped value the vocabulary lacks is `NotInCatalog`.
    pub fn resolve(&self, value: &str) -> Result<String, DenyReason> {
        let (name, path) = value.split_once('/').unwrap_or((value, ""));
        // `https://x/y` splits to the name `https:`, which is name-shaped; look at the whole
        // value for a scheme, and at the name for an IP literal with or without a port. A bare
        // hostname is indistinguishable from a name and comes back `NotInCatalog`, which is
        // coarse on purpose: neither reason describes the boundary.
        let address_shaped = value.contains("://")
            || name.parse::<IpAddr>().is_ok()
            || name.split(':').next().unwrap_or("").parse::<IpAddr>().is_ok();
        if address_shaped || check_capability_name(name).is_err() {
            return Err(DenyReason::NotACapability);
        }
        let host = self.names.get(name).ok_or(DenyReason::NotInCatalog)?;
        Ok(format!("https://{host}/{path}"))
    }

    /// Replace every destination property in a JSON Schema with the closed vocabulary.
    pub fn constrain_schema(&self, schema: &mut Value) {
        let Some(properties) = schema.get_mut("properties").and_then(Value::as_object_mut) else {
            return;
        };
        for key in DESTINATION_KEYS {
            if properties.contains_key(*key) {
                properties.insert(
                    (*key).to_string(),
                    json!({
                        "type": "string",
                        "enum": self.names(),
                        "description": "A destination capability from this warrant's catalog, \
                            optionally followed by /path. Raw hosts, IP addresses and URLs are not \
                            accepted and cannot be expressed here."
                    }),
                );
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
// ── every decision, written down ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/// Wire format of one recorded decision (allow or deny). Unsigned: the proxy holds no key.
pub const DECISION_FORMAT: &str = "warrantor.egress-decision/1";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct EgressDecision {
    pub format: String,
    pub warrant_id: String,
    pub at: u64,
    pub tool: String,
    pub argument: String,
    pub capability: String,
    pub destination: String,
    pub verdict: EgressVerdict,
    pub catalog_digest: Option<String>,
}

fn decision_path(root: &std::path::Path, warrant_id: &str) -> std::path::PathBuf {
    root.join("egress").join(format!("{warrant_id}.jsonl"))
}

/// Append decisions. Called BEFORE the call is forwarded; a failure here refuses the forward.
pub fn record_decisions(root: &std::path::Path, decisions: &[EgressDecision]) -> Result<usize, String> {
    use std::io::Write as _;
    let Some(first) = decisions.first() else {
        return Ok(0);
    };
    let path = decision_path(root, &first.warrant_id);
    std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap_or(root))
        .map_err(|e| format!("create the egress log directory: {e}"))?;
    let mut body = String::new();
    for decision in decisions {
        body.push_str(&serde_json::to_string(decision).map_err(|e| format!("encode: {e}"))?);
        body.push('\n');
    }
    let mut file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
        .create(true)
        .append(true)
        .open(&path)
        .map_err(|e| format!("open {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    file.write_all(body.as_bytes())
        .and_then(|()| file.sync_all())
        .map_err(|e| format!("append to {}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    Ok(decisions.len())
}

/// Every recorded decision for a warrant, and how many lines did not parse.
pub fn read_decisions(root: &std::path::Path, warrant_id: &str) -> Result<(Vec<EgressDecision>, usize), String> {
    let path = decision_path(root, warrant_id);
    let text = match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
        Ok(t) => t,
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok((Vec::new(), 0)),
        Err(e) => return Err(format!("read {}: {e}", path.display())),
    };
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut unreadable = 0;
    for line in text.lines().filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty()) {
        match serde_json::from_str::<EgressDecision>(line) {
            Ok(d) if d.format == DECISION_FORMAT => out.push(d),
            _ => unreadable += 1,
        }
    }
    Ok((out, unreadable))
}
```

Add methods:

```rust
    #[must_use]
    pub fn with_vocabulary(mut self, vocabulary: Vocabulary) -> Self {
        self.vocabulary = Some(vocabulary);
        self
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn vocabulary(&self) -> Option<&Vocabulary> {
        self.vocabulary.as_ref()
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn bounds(&self) -> &WarrantBounds {
        &self.bounds
    }

    /// Rewrite every destination-named argument from a capability name to its catalog URL.
    ///
    /// Under Enforce with a vocabulary, a raw address is refused here, before the broker — the
    /// L4-23 property: the argument has no way to say a host. Observe mode, or no vocabulary,
    /// leaves the call untouched and the host-based broker decides as before.
    pub fn resolve_destinations(&mut self, call: &mut ToolCall) -> Result<(), Decision> {
        self.resolved_names.clear();
        if self.mode != ProxyMode::Enforce {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let Some(vocabulary) = self.vocabulary.clone() else {
            return Ok(());
        };
        for key in DESTINATION_KEYS {
            let Some(value) = call.arguments.get(*key).cloned() else {
                continue;
            };
            let name = value.split_once('/').map_or(value.as_str(), |(n, _)| n);
            match vocabulary.resolve(&value) {
                Ok(url) => {
                    self.resolved_names
                        .insert(host_of(&url).to_string(), name.to_string());
                    call.arguments.insert((*key).to_string(), url);
                }
                Err(reason) => {
                    let destination = crate::egress::Destination {
                        argument: (*key).to_string(),
                        host: host_of(&value).to_string(),
                    };
                    let refusal = EgressRefusal::new(&call.tool, &destination, reason.clone());
                    self.pending.push(PendingDecision {
                        tool: call.tool.clone(),
                        argument: destination.argument.clone(),
                        capability: if reason == crate::egress::DenyReason::NotInCatalog {
                            name.to_string()
                        } else {
                            capability_for(&destination.host)
                        },
                        destination: destination.host.clone(),
                        verdict: EgressVerdict::Deny { reason },
                    });
                    return Err(self.deny_egress(&call.tool, refusal));
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Drain the decisions made since the last drain, stamped for the log.
    pub fn take_egress_decisions(&mut self, warrant_id: &str, at: u64) -> Vec<EgressDecision> {
        let digest = self.vocabulary.as_ref().map(|v| v.digest().to_string());
        std::mem::take(&mut self.pending)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|p| EgressDecision {
                format: crate::egress::DECISION_FORMAT.to_string(),
                warrant_id: warrant_id.to_string(),
                at,
                tool: p.tool,
                argument: p.argument,
                capability: p.capability,
                destination: p.destination,
                verdict: p.verdict,
                catalog_digest: digest.clone(),
            })
            .collect()
    }
```

```rust
/// The egress decisions this warrant's sessions recorded, each signed by the issuer at report time.
///
/// The proxy that made the decision holds no key, so the record it wrote is unsigned; this section
/// is that record countersigned by the issuer, with the decision's own timestamp. What it proves is
/// that these decisions were on disk when the report was taken. It does not prove the proxy saw
/// every connection the agent made — see `limitations`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct EgressSection {
    pub receipts: Vec<warrantor_egress::EgressReceipt>,
    pub unreadable_lines: usize,
    pub note: String,
}

pub fn egress_section(root: &std::path::Path, warrant_id: &str, issuer: &SigningKey, key_id: &str) -> Option<EgressSection> {
    let (decisions, unreadable_lines) = crate::egress::read_decisions(root, warrant_id).ok()?;
    if decisions.is_empty() && unreadable_lines == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let receipts = decisions
        .iter()
        .map(|d| {
            let request = warrantor_egress::EgressRequest {
                capability: d.capability.clone(),
                logical_endpoint: d.destination.clone(),
                chain_capabilities: Vec::new(),
                enforcement_mode: "advisory".to_string(),
                is_discovery: false,
                has_approval: false,
            };
            warrantor_egress::issue_receipt(&d.verdict, &request, d.at, issuer, key_id)
        })
        .collect();
    Some(EgressSection {
        receipts,
        unreadable_lines,
        note: "Signed by the issuer when the report was taken, over decisions the MCP proxy wrote \
               down before forwarding. Covers calls that traversed the proxy and nothing else."
            .to_string(),
    })
}
```

### Task 1.3: Containment and the kill switch into the `stop` verb; conformance receipt (L4-08, L0-03; `STOP_ENFORCEMENT_MODE` promotion)

**Anchor (plan-brief L4-08 / L0-03):** in the first hours of 20 July responders terminated six model-created pods, disabled 311 repositories used for message-board communication and removed 22 model-created administrator accounts (First-party · OpenAI S01 §VI.A); the CBUAE expects immediate shutdown of a third-party AI system with a 16 September 2026 compliance point (S43) and India's draft model-risk guidance requires an emergency kill switch (S78) — and L0-03's verification gate is "a single receipted kill halts every agent of a named family across every cluster within a stated bound, invalidates their leases, channel membership and task memory, and the revocation receipt verifies offline."

**What exists and what is wrong with it.** `rust/warrant/src/stop.rs` already terminates the supervisor's process group, holds the warrant, refuses new sessions, and writes a doubly-signed `SignedStop` scored by `warrantor_containment_conformance`. Three things keep it short of L4-08: (1) the kill it performs is `crate::supervise::terminate_group`, a fire-and-forget `taskkill`/`kill -KILL -pgid` with none of the safety rails, verified-gone polling or already-gone handling that `rust/kill-switch/src/execution.rs` built and tested — and that crate cannot be linked because its `Cargo.toml` declares `tokio`, `clap`, `tracing`, `tracing-subscriber` unconditionally; (2) `STOP_ENFORCEMENT_MODE` is the constant `"advisory"` on every kernel, so a kernel where the tree-kill has been observed to work is labeled the same as one where it has not, which fails Rule 2 in the *understating* direction; (3) stop reaches the process but not the task state — the warrant lands in `Held`, a state from which `Warrant::transition` still permits `Settled`, so a survivor holding the settle key can release what the halted agent staged. The `Held` reading was written for the *deadline* path and stays correct there; this task makes a *halt* terminal.

**Decision recorded, because it reverses a documented one.** `stop.rs` lines 29–31 say "Held, not Void: ending a run early is not misbehaviour, so the staged work is kept." The spine's acceptance for this task says `warrantor stop` "discards staged effects," and L4-08 says a stopped population "cannot be resumed by a survivor reading the board." A halt therefore transitions `Open | Held -> Void` through the existing `warrantor_warrant::settle::void_on_breach` (no settle key required — the same "3am" argument that function already carries). The hash-chained staged log is retained as evidence, which is exactly what `void` has always meant in this crate ("Staged effects discarded; receipts retained"). `WarrantState::Held` remains the outcome of the deadline path in `daemon.rs`, which this task does not touch.

```rust
//! The extraction is only worth doing if the extracted code still kills a real process tree.
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use warrantor_kill_switch_core::{process_exists, TreeKiller};

/// A root that spawns a descendant and writes the descendant's pid to `pid_file`, then waits.
fn spawn_tree(pid_file: &std::path::Path) -> std::process::Child {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    {
        let script = format!(
            "$p = Start-Process -FilePath ping -ArgumentList '-n','60','127.0.0.1' -WindowStyle Hidden -PassThru; \
             Set-Content -Path '{}' -Value $p.Id; Wait-Process -Id $p.Id",
            pid_file.display()
        );
        Command::new("powershell")
            .args(["-NoProfile", "-Command", &script])
            .stdout(Stdio::null())
            .spawn()
            .expect("spawn tree")
    }
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        Command::new("sh")
            .args(["-c", "sleep 60 & echo $! > \"$0\"; wait", &pid_file.display().to_string()])
            .stdout(Stdio::null())
            .spawn()
            .expect("spawn tree")
    }
}

fn read_pid(pid_file: &std::path::Path) -> u32 {
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10);
    while Instant::now() < deadline {
        if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(pid_file) {
            if let Ok(pid) = text.trim().parse::<u32>() {
                return pid;
            }
        }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
    }
    panic!("descendant pid never appeared in {}", pid_file.display());
}

#[test]
fn terminate_reaches_the_descendant_not_only_the_root() {
    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("wks-core-{}", std::process::id()));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).expect("tempdir");
    let pid_file = dir.join("descendant.pid");
    let mut root = spawn_tree(&pid_file);
    let descendant = read_pid(&pid_file);
    assert!(process_exists(root.id()) && process_exists(descendant));

    let terminated = TreeKiller::new().terminate(root.id()).expect("terminate");
    assert!(!terminated.already_gone);
    let _ = root.wait();
    assert!(!process_exists(root.id()), "root still alive");
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5);
    while process_exists(descendant) && Instant::now() < deadline {
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25));
    }
    assert!(!process_exists(descendant), "descendant {descendant} outlived the tree kill");
}

#[test]
fn reserved_and_self_pids_are_refused_before_any_helper_runs() {
    use warrantor_kill_switch_core::TerminateError;
    assert!(matches!(TreeKiller::new().terminate(0), Err(TerminateError::Reserved { pid: 0, .. })));
    assert!(matches!(
        TreeKiller::new().terminate(std::process::id()),
        Err(TerminateError::SelfTarget { .. })
    ));
}
```

```rust
//! Sync process-tree termination: the part of `warrantor-kill-switch` that a tokio-free crate can link.
#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
#![deny(missing_docs)]

use std::process::Command;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
use thiserror::Error;

/// How long to wait for a signalled process to actually disappear before declaring failure.
pub const TERMINATION_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
const TERMINATION_POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(20);

/// Why a termination did not happen. Every variant names the pid; none fabricates success.
#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum TerminateError {
    /// The pid is reserved on this platform and must never be signalled.
    #[error("refusing to signal pid {pid} ({reason})")]
    Reserved { /// The pid. 
        pid: u32, /// Why. 
        reason: &'static str },
    /// The pid is this process.
    #[error("refusing to signal the caller's own pid {pid}")]
    SelfTarget { /// The pid. 
        pid: u32 },
    /// The pid resolved to a critical Windows image.
    #[error("refusing to signal pid {pid} ({image} is a critical Windows process)")]
    CriticalImage { /// The pid. 
        pid: u32, /// The image name. 
        image: String },
    /// The platform helper could not be spawned.
    #[error("{what}: could not spawn helper: {source}")]
    Spawn { /// Which step. 
        what: String, /// The OS error. 
        source: std::io::Error },
    /// The helper ran and reported a failure that is not "already gone".
    #[error("{what}: helper exited {status} — {stderr}")]
    Helper { /// Which step. 
        what: String, /// Exit status text. 
        status: String, /// Trimmed stderr. 
        stderr: String },
    /// The process was signalled and is still present after the timeout.
    #[error("pid {pid} still alive {after:?} after the kill — containment NOT achieved")]
    StillAlive { /// The pid. 
        pid: u32, /// How long was waited. 
        after: Duration },
    /// No process-control primitive on this platform.
    #[error("no process-control primitive on this platform")]
    Unsupported,
}

/// What a successful termination observed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Terminated {
    /// The root pid.
    pub pid: u32,
    /// The root was gone before anything was sent.
    pub already_gone: bool,
    /// Time from the signal to the confirmed absence. Zero when already gone.
    pub confirmed_after: Duration,
}

/// A process-tree killer with the rails `LocalProcessEngine` had, minus the engine.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct TreeKiller {
    allow_self_target: bool,
    #[cfg_attr(not(windows), allow(dead_code))]
    critical_image_memo: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Option<(u32, Option<String>)>>>,
    #[cfg_attr(not(windows), allow(dead_code))]
    critical_image_lookups: std::sync::Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize>,
}

impl TreeKiller {
    /// Default rails.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new() -> Self { Self::default() }
    /// Permit targeting this process (tests only).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn allowing_self_target(mut self, allow: bool) -> Self { self.allow_self_target = allow; self }
    /// Run every rail. Cheap and deterministic first, `tasklist` last.
    pub fn checked_pid(&self, pid: u32) -> Result<u32, TerminateError> {
        if let Some(reason) = reserved_pid_reason(pid) { return Err(TerminateError::Reserved { pid, reason }); }
        if !self.allow_self_target && pid == std::process::id() { return Err(TerminateError::SelfTarget { pid }); }
        #[cfg(windows)]
        if let Some(image) = self.critical_image_cached(pid) { return Err(TerminateError::CriticalImage { pid, image }); }
        Ok(pid)
    }
    /// How many times the critical-image rail shelled out (tests assert the spawn count).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn critical_image_lookup_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.critical_image_lookups.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)
    }
    /// Kill `pid` and every descendant, then confirm the root is gone.
    ///
    /// Unix: `kill -KILL -- -pid` (the group; the supervisor's `setsid` makes pgid == pid) and then
    /// `kill -KILL pid` for a root that is not a group leader. Windows: `taskkill /PID pid /T /F`
    /// from `%SystemRoot%\System32`. Both then poll `process_exists` up to [`TERMINATION_TIMEOUT`].
    pub fn terminate(&self, pid: u32) -> Result<Terminated, TerminateError> {
        let pid = self.checked_pid(pid)?;
        if !process_exists(pid) {
            return Ok(Terminated { pid, already_gone: true, confirmed_after: Duration::ZERO });
        }
        let started = Instant::now();
        #[cfg(unix)]
        {
            let _ = send_signal_to(&format!("-{pid}"), "KILL", &format!("SIGKILL group {pid}"))?;
            if send_signal(pid, "KILL")? {
                return Ok(Terminated { pid, already_gone: true, confirmed_after: Duration::ZERO });
            }
        }
        #[cfg(windows)]
        {
            let what = format!("taskkill /T /F pid {pid}");
            let out = Command::new(system32_tool("taskkill.exe"))
                .args(["/PID", &pid.to_string(), "/T", "/F"])
                .output()
                .map_err(|source| TerminateError::Spawn { what: what.clone(), source })?;
            if !out.status.success() {
                let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).to_string();
                let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).to_string();
                if out.status.code() == Some(128) || stderr.contains("not found") || stdout.contains("not found") {
                    return Ok(Terminated { pid, already_gone: true, confirmed_after: Duration::ZERO });
                }
                return Err(TerminateError::Helper { what, status: out.status.to_string(), stderr: format!("{stderr}{stdout}").trim().to_string() });
            }
        }
        #[cfg(not(any(unix, windows)))]
        { return Err(TerminateError::Unsupported); }
        let deadline = started + TERMINATION_TIMEOUT;
        while Instant::now() < deadline {
            if !process_exists(pid) {
                return Ok(Terminated { pid, already_gone: false, confirmed_after: started.elapsed() });
            }
            std::thread::sleep(TERMINATION_POLL);
        }
        Err(TerminateError::StillAlive { pid, after: TERMINATION_TIMEOUT })
    }
}

/// Send `signal` to `pid`; `Ok(true)` means the target had already exited (ESRCH).
#[cfg(unix)]
pub fn send_signal(pid: u32, signal: &str) -> Result<bool, TerminateError> {
    send_signal_to(&pid.to_string(), signal, &format!("SIG{signal} pid {pid}"))
}

#[cfg(unix)]
fn send_signal_to(target: &str, signal: &str, what: &str) -> Result<bool, TerminateError> {
    let out = Command::new("kill")
        .args([&format!("-{signal}"), "--", target])
        .output()
        .map_err(|source| TerminateError::Spawn { what: what.to_string(), source })?;
    if out.status.success() { return Ok(false); }
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr);
    if stderr_means_already_gone(&stderr) { return Ok(true); }
    Err(TerminateError::Helper { what: what.to_string(), status: out.status.to_string(), stderr: stderr.trim().to_string() })
}
// process_exists, reserved_pid_reason, WINDOWS_CRITICAL_IMAGES, image_name_from_tasklist_row,
// windows_critical_image, critical_image_cached, stderr_means_already_gone, system32_tool: moved
// verbatim from rust/kill-switch/src/execution.rs (bodies unchanged; `reserved_pid_reason` and
// `process_exists` become `pub`). The `safety_rail_tests` module moves here unchanged.
```

```rust
//! `warrantor stop` against a REAL supervised tree, on every kernel CI runs. This is the observed
//! refusal Rule 2 requires before `Enforced` may be claimed for the stop path on that kernel.
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
use warrantor_kill_switch_core::process_exists;
use warrantor_warrant::daemon::DaemonRecord;
use warrantor_warrant::stop::{self, OsProcessControl, STOP_BUDGET};
use warrantor_warrant::store::StoredWarrant;
use warrantor_warrant::supervise::Supervisor;
use warrantor_warrant::{SideEffectClass, Warrant, WarrantBounds, WarrantState};

const NOW: u64 = 1_786_000_000;

fn stored() -> StoredWarrant {
    let bounds = WarrantBounds {
        tools: ["git".to_string()].into_iter().collect(),
        write_paths: ["src/**".to_string()].into_iter().collect(),
        egress_hosts: Default::default(),
        staged_classes: [SideEffectClass::Write].into_iter().collect(),
        expires_at: NOW + 3600,
        budget_cents_observed: None,
        delegation_depth: 2,
    };
    let warrant = Warrant::grant("wrt_tree", "drill", "spiffe://muveraai.com/agent/drill", bounds, NOW,
        &SigningKey::from_bytes(&[2; 32]).verifying_key(), &SigningKey::from_bytes(&[1; 32])).expect("grant");
    StoredWarrant { warrant, worktree: None, repo: None, branch: None, base_commit: None, staged_chain: None }
}

/// Spawn the same root/descendant pair the core test uses, under the real Supervisor link.
fn spawn_tree(supervisor: &mut Supervisor, pid_file: &Path) -> u32 {
    #[cfg(windows)]
    let (program, args) = ("powershell", vec!["-NoProfile".to_string(), "-Command".to_string(), format!(
        "$p = Start-Process -FilePath ping -ArgumentList '-n','60','127.0.0.1' -WindowStyle Hidden -PassThru; \
         Set-Content -Path '{}' -Value $p.Id; Wait-Process -Id $p.Id", pid_file.display())]);
    #[cfg(unix)]
    let (program, args) = ("sh", vec!["-c".to_string(), "sleep 60 & echo $! > \"$0\"; wait".to_string(), pid_file.display().to_string()]);
    supervisor.spawn(program, &args, None).expect("spawn tree")
}

fn read_pid(pid_file: &Path) -> u32 {
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10);
    while Instant::now() < deadline {
        if let Some(pid) = std::fs::read_to_string(pid_file).ok().and_then(|t| t.trim().parse().ok()) { return pid; }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));
    }
    panic!("no descendant pid");
}

#[test]
fn stop_kills_the_supervised_tree_within_budget_and_voids_the_warrant() {
    let dir: PathBuf = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("warrantor-tree-{}", std::process::id()));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).expect("tempdir");
    let mut supervisor = Supervisor::new().expect("link");
    let root_pid = spawn_tree(&mut supervisor, &dir.join("descendant.pid"));
    let descendant = read_pid(&dir.join("descendant.pid"));
    assert!(process_exists(root_pid) && process_exists(descendant));

    let record = DaemonRecord { warrant_id: "wrt_tree".into(), pid: root_pid, socket: PathBuf::new(), started_at: NOW, expires_at: NOW + 3600 };
    let mut warrant = stored();
    let started = Instant::now();
    let outcome = stop::execute(&mut warrant, Some(&record), &OsProcessControl, &dir.join("wrt_tree.jsonl"), None, NOW);
    let _ = supervisor.wait();

    assert!(outcome.supervisor_gone, "root {root_pid} did not die");
    assert!(started.elapsed() <= STOP_BUDGET + Duration::from_millis(500), "stop overran STOP_BUDGET: {:?}", started.elapsed());
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(2);
    while process_exists(descendant) && Instant::now() < deadline { std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)); }
    assert!(!process_exists(descendant), "descendant {descendant} survived the stop");
    assert_eq!(outcome.state_after, WarrantState::Void, "a halt is terminal");
    assert!(outcome.invalidated.iter().any(|i| matches!(i, stop::Invalidation::StagedEffects { .. })));
    assert_eq!(stop::enforcement_mode(&outcome), stop::EnforcementMode::Advisory, "no receipt was supplied, so no promotion");
}
```

```rust
/// How strongly this kernel's kill path is known to hold. Never a constant: read from a
/// `warrantor conformance run` receipt for THIS kernel, or `Advisory` when there is none.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum EnforcementMode { /// No drill receipt for this kernel; the kill is best-effort. 
    Advisory, /// A drill on this kernel observed the tree die within budget. 
    Enforced }
impl EnforcementMode {
    /// The word written into the conformance report's `enforcement_mode`.
    #[must_use] pub const fn word(self) -> &'static str { match self { Self::Advisory => "advisory", Self::Enforced => "enforced" } }
}
/// Why a record says `enforced`: which receipt, for which kernel, drilled when.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct EnforcementBasis { /// `conformance::kernel_id()` at drill time. 
    pub kernel: String, /// `SignedConformanceReceipt::receipt_digest`. 
    pub receipt_digest: String, /// Epoch seconds. 
    pub drilled_at: u64 }
/// One thing a halt reached beyond the process. Observations, not intentions.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Invalidation {
    /// New capability leases are refused; leases already minted expire by `outstanding_until`.
    CapabilityLeases { /// The warrant. 
        warrant_id: String, /// `now + CAPABILITY_TTL_SECONDS`. 
        outstanding_until: u64 },
    /// A new supervised MCP session is refused (observed via `agent_endpoint_for`).
    SessionMembership { /// The warrant. 
        warrant_id: String },
    /// Staged effects can no longer be released: the warrant is Void. The log is kept as evidence.
    StagedEffects { /// The warrant. 
        warrant_id: String, /// Effects in the log. 
        count: u64, /// The chain head at halt. 
        chain_head: String, /// Where the log still is. 
        log_retained_at: String },
    /// The worktree was removed.
    Worktree { /// Its path. 
        path: String },
}
/// The mode a record carries, derived from its basis so the two cannot disagree.
#[must_use]
pub fn enforcement_mode(outcome: &StopOutcome) -> EnforcementMode {
    if outcome.enforcement.is_some() { EnforcementMode::Enforced } else { EnforcementMode::Advisory }
}
```

```rust
    let signed = conformance::sign_receipt(&drill, &issuer(), 1).expect("sign");
    assert_eq!(signed.receipt.mode, EnforcementMode::Advisory, "sign_receipt derives the mode; it does not accept one");
    let mut forged = signed.clone();
    forged.receipt.mode = EnforcementMode::Enforced;
    assert!(matches!(conformance::verify_receipt(&forged), Err(StopError::Digest { .. })));
}

#[test]
fn a_stop_is_promoted_only_by_a_verified_receipt_for_this_kernel() {
    let dir = tempdir("promote");
    let store = ConformanceStore::open(&dir).expect("store");
    assert!(store.basis_for_this_kernel().is_none());
    let signed = conformance::sign_receipt(&conformance::drill(&dir).expect("drill"), &issuer(), 7).expect("sign");
    store.save(&signed).expect("save");
    let basis = store.basis_for_this_kernel().expect("promoted");
    assert_eq!(basis.receipt_digest, signed.receipt_digest);
    // A receipt for another kernel promotes nothing here.
    let mut elsewhere = signed.clone();
    elsewhere.receipt.kernel = "plan9/none".to_string();
    let other = ConformanceStore::open(tempdir("elsewhere")).expect("store");
    other.save(&elsewhere).expect("save");
    assert!(other.basis_for_this_kernel().is_none());
    let _ = stop::STOP_BUDGET;
}
```

```rust
//! `warrantor conformance run` — the drill that earns a kernel its `enforced` label (L0-03).
//!
//! A real root+descendant tree is spawned under the real [`Supervisor`] link, killed through
//! `warrantor_kill_switch_core::TreeKiller`, and both pids are polled until gone. The receipt
//! records what was observed and derives `mode` from it; nobody supplies the mode. The suite's
//! anti-sandbagging rule is untouched: warrantor elicits no resistance, so every pass-like verdict
//! is still downgraded — `mode` is a statement about the kill path, never about an adversary.
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
use ed25519_dalek::{Signature, Signer, SigningKey, Verifier};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use warrantor_containment_conformance as suite;
use warrantor_kill_switch_core::{process_exists, TreeKiller};
use crate::report::{canonicalize, sha256_hex};
use crate::stop::{EnforcementBasis, EnforcementMode, StopError, STOP_BUDGET};
use crate::supervise::{describe_linkage, Supervisor};

/// Wire format of [`SignedConformanceReceipt`].
pub const CONFORMANCE_RECEIPT_FORMAT: &str = "warrantor.containment-conformance/1";
const RECEIPT_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"warrantor-containment-conformance-v1";
const POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(25);

/// `"<os>/<linkage>"`, e.g. `linux/setsid+pdeathsig`, `windows/job-object`.
#[must_use]
pub fn kernel_id() -> String { format!("{}/{}", std::env::consts::OS, describe_linkage().mechanism) }

/// What the drill saw.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DrillObservation {
    /// The supervised root. 
    pub root_pid: u32,
    /// A descendant the root spawned. 
    pub descendant_pid: u32,
    /// Trigger to confirmed root absence. 
    pub trigger_to_root_gone_ms: u64,
    /// Trigger to confirmed descendant absence. 
    pub trigger_to_descendant_gone_ms: u64,
    /// The root was confirmed gone within [`STOP_BUDGET`]. 
    pub root_gone: bool,
    /// The descendant was confirmed gone within [`STOP_BUDGET`]. 
    pub descendant_gone: bool,
    /// Both within budget. 
    pub within_budget: bool,
    /// A rail refusal or helper error, verbatim, when the kill was not attempted or failed. 
    pub refusal: Option<String>,
}

/// Run the drill. `scratch` receives the descendant pid file.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`StopError::Encode`] when the tree cannot be spawned or the descendant pid never appears.
pub fn drill(scratch: &Path) -> Result<DrillObservation, StopError> {
    let pid_file = scratch.join(format!("drill-{}.pid", std::process::id()));
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&pid_file);
    let mut supervisor = Supervisor::new().map_err(StopError::Encode)?;
    #[cfg(windows)]
    let (program, args) = ("powershell", vec!["-NoProfile".to_string(), "-Command".to_string(), format!(
        "$p = Start-Process -FilePath ping -ArgumentList '-n','60','127.0.0.1' -WindowStyle Hidden -PassThru; \
         Set-Content -Path '{}' -Value $p.Id; Wait-Process -Id $p.Id", pid_file.display())]);
    #[cfg(not(windows))]
    let (program, args) = ("sh", vec!["-c".to_string(), "sleep 60 & echo $! > \"$0\"; wait".to_string(), pid_file.display().to_string()]);
    let root_pid = supervisor.spawn(program, &args, None).map_err(StopError::Encode)?;
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10);
    let descendant_pid = loop {
        if let Some(pid) = std::fs::read_to_string(&pid_file).ok().and_then(|t| t.trim().parse::<u32>().ok()) { break pid; }
        if Instant::now() >= deadline { let _ = supervisor.terminate(); return Err(StopError::Encode("the drill's descendant never reported its pid".into())); }
        std::thread::sleep(POLL);
    };
    let started = Instant::now();
    let refusal = TreeKiller::new().terminate(root_pid).err().map(|e| e.to_string());
    let mut root_gone_at = None; let mut descendant_gone_at = None;
    while started.elapsed() < STOP_BUDGET && (root_gone_at.is_none() || descendant_gone_at.is_none()) {
        if root_gone_at.is_none() && !process_exists(root_pid) { root_gone_at = Some(started.elapsed()); }
        if descendant_gone_at.is_none() && !process_exists(descendant_pid) { descendant_gone_at = Some(started.elapsed()); }
        std::thread::sleep(POLL);
    }
    let _ = supervisor.wait();
    let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&pid_file);
    let ms = |d: Option<Duration>| d.map_or(u64::MAX, |d| u64::try_from(d.as_millis()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX));
    Ok(DrillObservation {
        root_pid, descendant_pid,
        trigger_to_root_gone_ms: ms(root_gone_at), trigger_to_descendant_gone_ms: ms(descendant_gone_at),
        root_gone: root_gone_at.is_some(), descendant_gone: descendant_gone_at.is_some(),
        within_budget: root_gone_at.is_some() && descendant_gone_at.is_some(), refusal,
    })
}

/// The mode a drill earns. The ONLY place a mode is decided.
#[must_use]
pub fn mode_for(drill: &DrillObservation) -> EnforcementMode {
    if drill.root_gone && drill.descendant_gone && drill.within_budget && drill.refusal.is_none() { EnforcementMode::Enforced } else { EnforcementMode::Advisory }
}

/// The receipt body.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ConformanceReceipt {
    /// [`kernel_id`] at drill time. 
    pub kernel: String,
    /// `warrantor-warrant/<version>`. 
    pub subject_version: String,
    /// Epoch seconds. 
    pub drilled_at: u64,
    /// The observation. 
    pub drill: DrillObservation,
    /// Derived by [`mode_for`]. 
    pub mode: EnforcementMode,
    /// The suite's own signed report over the same observation. 
    pub report: suite::SignedConformanceReport,
}

/// A receipt plus warrantor's signature over it (same two-signature shape as `SignedStop`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SignedConformanceReceipt {
    /// [`CONFORMANCE_RECEIPT_FORMAT`]. 
    pub format: String,
    /// SHA-256 hex of the canonical receipt. 
    pub receipt_digest: String,
    /// The receipt. 
    pub receipt: ConformanceReceipt,
    /// `Ed25519`. 
    pub signature_algorithm: String,
    /// Hex verifying key. 
    pub signature_public_key: String,
    /// Hex signature over the domain-separated digest. 
    pub signature_value: String,
}

fn suite_report(drill: &DrillObservation, mode: EnforcementMode, now: u64) -> Result<suite::ContainmentConformanceReport, StopError> {
    use suite::{CapabilityResult as R, ContainmentCapability as C, Verdict as V};
    let stop = if mode == EnforcementMode::Enforced { V::PassWithCaveats } else { V::Fail };
    let caps = vec![
        R { capability: C::StopInference, verdict: stop, trigger_to_quiescence_p50_ms: drill.trigger_to_descendant_gone_ms, trigger_to_quiescence_p99_ms: drill.trigger_to_descendant_gone_ms, assertion_hold: drill.within_budget, escape_attempts_blocked: 0, escape_attempts_total: 0,
            caveats: vec![format!("root pid {} gone in {} ms, descendant pid {} gone in {} ms; single trial", drill.root_pid, drill.trigger_to_root_gone_ms, drill.descendant_pid, drill.trigger_to_descendant_gone_ms)] },
        R { capability: C::TerminateAccess, verdict: V::Unscored, trigger_to_quiescence_p50_ms: 0, trigger_to_quiescence_p99_ms: 0, assertion_hold: false, escape_attempts_blocked: 0, escape_attempts_total: 0, caveats: vec!["the drill has no warrant, so access revocation is scored by each stop record, not here".into()] },
        R { capability: C::SuspendPattern, verdict: V::Unscored, trigger_to_quiescence_p50_ms: 0, trigger_to_quiescence_p99_ms: 0, assertion_hold: false, escape_attempts_blocked: 0, escape_attempts_total: 0, caveats: vec!["warrantor has no account or use-pattern concept".into()] },
        R { capability: C::FullShutdown, verdict: V::Unscored, trigger_to_quiescence_p50_ms: 0, trigger_to_quiescence_p99_ms: 0, assertion_hold: false, escape_attempts_blocked: 0, escape_attempts_total: 0, caveats: vec!["one tree was drilled; `stop --family` halts many warrants but no all-machine verb exists".into()] },
    ];
    suite::finalize_report(suite::ContainmentConformanceReport {
        subject_system: format!("warrantor kill path on {}", kernel_id()),
        subject_version: format!("warrantor-warrant/{}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")),
        enforcement_mode: mode.word().to_string(), capabilities: caps, elicitation: None,
        limitations: vec![
            "The drilled tree was cooperative: no agent was instructed to resist, so the suite downgrades every pass-like verdict. `mode` describes the kill path, not an adversary.".into(),
            "A grandchild that re-parents itself out of the session/job before the kill is not individually signalled on Linux; the drill's descendant does not do that.".into(),
            "There is no network namespace, seccomp filter or firewall; the drill establishes nothing about egress.".into(),
        ],
        timestamp: now, suite_version: suite::SUITE_VERSION.to_string(),
    }).map_err(|e| StopError::Conformance(e.to_string()))
}

fn digest(receipt: &ConformanceReceipt) -> Result<String, StopError> {
    let value = serde_json::to_value(receipt).map_err(|e| StopError::Encode(format!("serialise receipt: {e}")))?;
    let text = serde_json::to_string(&canonicalize(&value)).map_err(|e| StopError::Encode(format!("canonical receipt: {e}")))?;
    Ok(sha256_hex(text.as_bytes()))
}

/// Sign a drill into a receipt. The mode is derived here, never accepted.
pub fn sign_receipt(drill: &DrillObservation, key: &SigningKey, now: u64) -> Result<SignedConformanceReceipt, StopError> {
    let mode = mode_for(drill);
    let receipt = ConformanceReceipt { kernel: kernel_id(), subject_version: format!("warrantor-warrant/{}", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")), drilled_at: now, drill: drill.clone(), mode, report: suite::sign_report(&suite_report(drill, mode, now)?, key) };
    let receipt_digest = digest(&receipt)?;
    let signature = key.sign(&signing_input(receipt_digest.as_bytes()));
    Ok(SignedConformanceReceipt { format: CONFORMANCE_RECEIPT_FORMAT.into(), receipt_digest, receipt, signature_algorithm: "Ed25519".into(), signature_public_key: hex::encode(key.verifying_key().to_bytes()), signature_value: hex::encode(signature.to_bytes()) })
}

fn signing_input(body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(RECEIPT_DOMAIN.len() + body.len() + 16);
    out.extend_from_slice(&(RECEIPT_DOMAIN.len() as u64).to_le_bytes()); out.extend_from_slice(RECEIPT_DOMAIN);
    out.extend_from_slice(&(body.len() as u64).to_le_bytes()); out.extend_from_slice(body); out
}

/// Offline check: format, digest, both signatures, one key, mode derived from the observation.
pub fn verify_receipt(signed: &SignedConformanceReceipt) -> Result<(), StopError> {
    if signed.format != CONFORMANCE_RECEIPT_FORMAT { return Err(StopError::Format { found: signed.format.clone(), expected: CONFORMANCE_RECEIPT_FORMAT }); }
    let actual = digest(&signed.receipt)?;
    if actual != signed.receipt_digest { return Err(StopError::Digest { expected: signed.receipt_digest.clone(), actual }); }
    let raw = hex::decode(&signed.signature_public_key).map_err(|e| StopError::Signature(format!("public key hex: {e}")))?;
    let bytes: [u8; 32] = raw.as_slice().try_into().map_err(|_| StopError::Signature("public key must be 32 bytes".into()))?;
    let key = ed25519_dalek::VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&bytes).map_err(|e| StopError::Signature(format!("public key: {e}")))?;
    let raw = hex::decode(&signed.signature_value).map_err(|e| StopError::Signature(format!("signature hex: {e}")))?;
    let bytes: [u8; 64] = raw.as_slice().try_into().map_err(|_| StopError::Signature("signature must be 64 bytes".into()))?;
    key.verify(&signing_input(signed.receipt_digest.as_bytes()), &Signature::from_bytes(&bytes)).map_err(|_| StopError::Signature("the receipt's signature does not verify".into()))?;
    suite::verify_signed_report(&signed.receipt.report).map_err(|e| StopError::Signature(format!("conformance report: {e}")))?;
    if signed.receipt.report.signature_public_key != signed.signature_public_key { return Err(StopError::Binding("the suite report and the receipt were signed by different keys".into())); }
    if signed.receipt.mode != mode_for(&signed.receipt.drill) { return Err(StopError::OverClaim(format!("mode {:?} is not what the recorded drill earns", signed.receipt.mode))); }
    if signed.receipt.report.report.enforcement_mode != signed.receipt.mode.word() { return Err(StopError::Binding("the suite report's enforcement_mode disagrees with the receipt".into())); }
    if signed.receipt.report.report.elicitation.is_some() { return Err(StopError::OverClaim("a drill receipt carries no elicitation".into())); }
    Ok(())
}

/// `<root>/conformance/<kernel>.json`, one receipt per kernel.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ConformanceStore { root: PathBuf }
impl ConformanceStore {
    /// Open or create. 
    pub fn open(root: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<Self, StopError> {
        let root = root.as_ref().join("conformance");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&root).map_err(|e| StopError::Encode(format!("create conformance dir: {e}")))?;
        Ok(Self { root })
    }
    fn path(&self, kernel: &str) -> PathBuf { self.root.join(format!("{}.json", kernel.replace(['/', '+'], "-"))) }
    /// Persist. 
    pub fn save(&self, signed: &SignedConformanceReceipt) -> Result<PathBuf, StopError> {
        let path = self.path(&signed.receipt.kernel);
        let body = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(signed).map_err(|e| StopError::Encode(format!("serialise receipt: {e}")))?;
        std::fs::write(&path, body).map_err(|e| StopError::Encode(format!("write {}: {e}", path.display())))?;
        Ok(path)
    }
    /// Read one kernel's receipt, when it exists and parses. 
    #[must_use]
    pub fn get(&self, kernel: &str) -> Option<SignedConformanceReceipt> { serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(self.path(kernel)).ok()?).ok() }
    /// The basis a stop record on THIS kernel may cite: a receipt that verifies, is for this kernel, and earned `Enforced`. 
    #[must_use]
    pub fn basis_for_this_kernel(&self) -> Option<EnforcementBasis> {
        let kernel = kernel_id();
        let signed = self.get(&kernel)?;
        (verify_receipt(&signed).is_ok() && signed.receipt.kernel == kernel && signed.receipt.mode == EnforcementMode::Enforced)
            .then(|| EnforcementBasis { kernel, receipt_digest: signed.receipt_digest.clone(), drilled_at: signed.receipt.drilled_at })
    }
}
```
