```rust
/// One tool's decomposition into syscalls. Fields are private so a decomposition with no
/// syscalls — which would project to `Read` by accident — cannot be constructed.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Decomposition {
    tool: String,
    syscalls: BTreeSet<Syscall>,
}

impl Decomposition {
    /// Build a decomposition. Refuses an empty tool name and an empty set.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// A sentence naming what was wrong, suitable for the command line.
    pub fn new(tool: &str, syscalls: BTreeSet<Syscall>) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let tool = tool.trim();
        if tool.is_empty() {
            return Err("a decomposition names no tool".to_string());
        }
        if syscalls.is_empty() {
            return Err(format!(
                "{tool} decomposes to nothing; a tool with no effect is a tool nobody needs to \
                 declare, and one with an effect must say which"
            ));
        }
        Ok(Self {
            tool: tool.to_string(),
            syscalls,
        })
    }

    /// Parse `<tool>=<verb>+<verb>...`. The LAST `=` splits, so a tool name may not contain one
    /// and a verb list never does.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// The first thing wrong with the value, naming the nine verbs when the fault is a verb. A
    /// typo is refused rather than defaulted: a misspelled `mutate` forwarded as a read is the
    /// exact failure this registry exists to end.
    pub fn parse(raw: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let Some((tool, verbs)) = raw.rsplit_once('=') else {
            return Err(format!(
                "--upstream-effects takes tool=verb+verb, e.g. --upstream-effects \
                 'deploy.to_prod=exec+net+mutate'; got {raw:?}"
            ));
        };
        let tool = tool.trim();
        if tool.is_empty() {
            return Err(format!("--upstream-effects {raw:?} names no tool"));
        }
        if verbs.trim().is_empty() {
            return Err(format!(
                "{tool} decomposes to nothing; a tool with no effect is a tool nobody needs to \
                 declare, and one with an effect must say which"
            ));
        }
        let mut syscalls = BTreeSet::new();
        for word in verbs.split('+') {
            let word = word.trim();
            let Some(syscall) = Syscall::parse(word) else {
                return Err(format!(
                    "{word:?} is not an effect syscall. The nine are: {}. Refusing rather than \
                     defaulting -- a typo here would forward an effect the warrant never decided.",
                    verb_list()
                ));
            };
            if !syscalls.insert(syscall) {
                return Err(format!("{tool} lists {word} twice; a decomposition is a set"));
            }
        }
        Self::new(tool, syscalls)
    }

    /// The published tool name, `<server>.<tool>`.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn tool(&self) -> &str {
        &self.tool
    }

    /// The syscalls, in table order.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn syscalls(&self) -> &BTreeSet<Syscall> {
        &self.syscalls
    }

    /// The class the proxy decides by, until staging moves onto syscalls: the highest-ranked
    /// projection of any syscall present. Never lower than any member.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn class(&self) -> SideEffectClass {
        let mut best = SideEffectClass::Read;
        for syscall in &self.syscalls {
            let class = syscall.projection();
            if rank(class) > rank(best) {
                best = class;
            }
        }
        best
    }

    /// `verb+verb` in set order, so equal decompositions render equal.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn render(&self) -> String {
        self.syscalls
            .iter()
            .map(|s| s.as_str())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("+")
    }
}
```

```rust
    let error = DecompositionRegistry::from_json(&empty).expect_err("refused");
    assert!(error.contains("decomposes to nothing"), "{error}");
```

```rust
/// What the registry says about one tool.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Classified<'a> {
    /// Somebody declared it.
    Declared(&'a Decomposition),
    /// Nobody declared it and the policy is [`UnclassifiedPolicy::GuessRead`]: the caller uses
    /// `Read` and must name the tool at the end of the session, because a count is not a work
    /// list.
    Guessed,
}

/// What to do with a tool nobody declared.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum UnclassifiedPolicy {
    /// Strict mode: refuse the call. What `--upstream-strict` selects.
    Refuse,
    /// The shipped default until Task 2.2 lands signed manifests: class it `Read`, forward it,
    /// and name it when the session ends.
    GuessRead,
}

/// A tool refused under [`UnclassifiedPolicy::Refuse`]. `Display` is the sentence the agent
/// reads, and it tells the operator what to type.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Unclassified {
    /// The published tool name.
    pub tool: String,
}

impl std::fmt::Display for Unclassified {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(
            f,
            "{} has no declared effect decomposition, and this session is strict. This build can \
             only tell what a call DOES for the tools it stages; for everything else the \
             decomposition is what an operator declared, and an undeclared tool would otherwise be \
             forwarded as if it only read. Declare it: --upstream-effects '{}=mutate' (verbs: {}, \
             joined with '+'), or load a {EFFECT_REGISTRY_FORMAT} file with \
             --upstream-effects-file <path>.",
            self.tool,
            self.tool,
            verb_list()
        )
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for Unclassified {}

/// The on-disk shape of [`EFFECT_REGISTRY_FORMAT`]. Deliberately a map of verb lists rather than
/// of [`Decomposition`]s, so the only way in is through [`Decomposition::new`]'s checks.
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct RegistryDocument {
    format: String,
    tools: BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<Syscall>>,
}

/// Published tool name → decomposition.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DecompositionRegistry {
    tools: BTreeMap<String, Decomposition>,
}

impl DecompositionRegistry {
    /// An empty registry.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }

    /// The four tools this build can stage and perform, as [`crate::staging::EffectRegistry::github`]
    /// lists them. Exactly these and no more: a builtin decomposition for a tool the settle path
    /// cannot perform would promise staging that never happens.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn builtin() -> Self {
        fn of(tool: &str, syscalls: &[Syscall]) -> Decomposition {
            Decomposition {
                tool: tool.to_string(),
                syscalls: syscalls.iter().copied().collect(),
            }
        }
        let mut registry = Self::new();
        for decomposition in [
            of("github.create_pr", &[Syscall::Net, Syscall::Mutate]),
            of("github.comment", &[Syscall::Net, Syscall::Msg]),
            of("github.request_review", &[Syscall::Net, Syscall::Msg]),
            of("github.add_label", &[Syscall::Net, Syscall::Mutate]),
        ] {
            registry
                .tools
                .insert(decomposition.tool.clone(), decomposition);
        }
        registry
    }

    /// Add one declaration. A second declaration for the same tool is refused even when identical:
    /// on one command line, saying a thing twice is a sign one of the two was meant to be
    /// something else.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// The duplicate, with both decompositions named.
    pub fn insert(&mut self, decomposition: Decomposition) -> Result<(), String> {
        if let Some(existing) = self.tools.get(&decomposition.tool) {
            return Err(format!(
                "{} is declared twice ({} and {}). Two decompositions for one tool means \
                 whichever was read last decides what happens to it, which is not a decision \
                 anybody made.",
                decomposition.tool,
                existing.render(),
                decomposition.render()
            ));
        }
        self.tools
            .insert(decomposition.tool.clone(), decomposition);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Fold `other` in. An identical redeclaration is accepted (two documents may both state the
    /// obvious); a different one is refused, and the existing decomposition is named so the
    /// operator can see which side is wrong.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// The first conflict.
    pub fn merge(&mut self, other: Self) -> Result<(), String> {
        for (tool, decomposition) in other.tools {
            match self.tools.get(&tool) {
                Some(existing) if *existing == decomposition => {}
                Some(existing) => {
                    return Err(format!(
                        "{tool} is already declared as {} and cannot be redeclared as {}. If the \
                         existing one is builtin, it is what the settle path actually performs; \
                         if it came from a file, fix the file.",
                        existing.render(),
                        decomposition.render()
                    ))
                }
                None => {
                    self.tools.insert(tool, decomposition);
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Look a tool up.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn get(&self, tool: &str) -> Option<&Decomposition> {
        self.tools.get(tool)
    }

    /// How many tools are declared.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.tools.len()
    }

    /// Whether nothing is declared.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.tools.is_empty()
    }

    /// Read a [`EFFECT_REGISTRY_FORMAT`] document. Any other format is refused by name; a
    /// document with no `format` field is not a registry at all.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// The parse failure, the foreign format, or the first bad decomposition inside.
    pub fn from_json(body: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let document: RegistryDocument = serde_json::from_str(body)
            .map_err(|e| format!("not a {EFFECT_REGISTRY_FORMAT} document: {e}"))?;
        if document.format != EFFECT_REGISTRY_FORMAT {
            return Err(format!(
                "format {:?} is not {EFFECT_REGISTRY_FORMAT}. A registry in another format is not \
                 read, it is refused; a new format gets a new name, never a silent change.",
                document.format
            ));
        }
        let mut registry = Self::new();
        for (tool, syscalls) in document.tools {
            registry.insert(Decomposition::new(&tool, syscalls)?)?;
        }
        Ok(registry)
    }

    /// Render as a [`EFFECT_REGISTRY_FORMAT`] document, tools in name order.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// Only a serialization failure, which for this shape does not occur.
    pub fn to_json(&self) -> Result<String, String> {
        let document = RegistryDocument {
            format: EFFECT_REGISTRY_FORMAT.to_string(),
            tools: self
                .tools
                .iter()
                .map(|(tool, d)| (tool.clone(), d.syscalls.clone()))
                .collect(),
        };
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(&document).map_err(|e| format!("encode registry: {e}"))
    }

    /// Classify one published tool under `policy`.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`Unclassified`] when nobody declared the tool and the policy is
    /// [`UnclassifiedPolicy::Refuse`].
    pub fn classify(
        &self,
        tool: &str,
        policy: UnclassifiedPolicy,
    ) -> Result<Classified<'_>, Unclassified> {
        match (self.tools.get(tool), policy) {
            (Some(decomposition), _) => Ok(Classified::Declared(decomposition)),
            (None, UnclassifiedPolicy::GuessRead) => Ok(Classified::Guessed),
            (None, UnclassifiedPolicy::Refuse) => Err(Unclassified {
                tool: tool.to_string(),
            }),
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
/// One row of the corpus. `expected` is a verb list for a declared tool or the word `refuse`.
#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
struct CorpusRow {
    tool: String,
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    input_schema: serde_json::Value,
    expected: serde_json::Value,
}

/// The B-04 gate: present the registry with a corpus of tool schemas it has never seen the
/// schemas of; every declared tool classifies to exactly its declared verbs, every undeclared
/// tool is refused under strict mode, and nothing is defaulted. There is no classifier under
/// test: the schema column exists to prove that nothing in it is consulted, which is the point.
#[test]
fn the_corpus_classifies_by_declaration_and_refuses_every_unseen_tool_under_strict_mode() {
    let registry = DecompositionRegistry::from_json(include_str!("fixtures/effect-registry.json"))
        .expect("the fixture registry reads");
    let corpus = include_str!("fixtures/tool-schemas.jsonl");
    let mut declared = 0usize;
    let mut refused = 0usize;
    for line in corpus.lines().filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty()) {
        let row: CorpusRow = serde_json::from_str(line).expect(line);
        let verdict = registry.classify(&row.tool, UnclassifiedPolicy::Refuse);
        match row.expected {
            serde_json::Value::String(ref word) if word == "refuse" => {
                let refusal = verdict.expect_err(&row.tool);
                assert_eq!(refusal.tool, row.tool);
                refused += 1;
            }
            serde_json::Value::Array(ref verbs) => {
                let expected: BTreeSet<Syscall> = verbs
                    .iter()
                    .map(|v| Syscall::parse(v.as_str().expect("verb")).expect("a known verb"))
                    .collect();
                match verdict {
                    Ok(Classified::Declared(d)) => assert_eq!(d.syscalls(), &expected, "{}", row.tool),
                    other => panic!("{} should be declared: {other:?}", row.tool),
                }
                declared += 1;
            }
            other => panic!("{}: bad expectation {other}", row.tool),
        }
    }
    assert_eq!((declared, refused), (20, 6), "the corpus shape is part of the test");
    // Under the shipped policy the same six are guesses, and every guess is visible as one.
    let guessed = corpus
        .lines()
        .filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty())
        .map(|l| serde_json::from_str::<CorpusRow>(l).expect(l).tool)
        .filter(|t| registry.classify(t, UnclassifiedPolicy::GuessRead) == Ok(Classified::Guessed))
        .count();
    assert_eq!(guessed, 6);
    eprintln!("effect-registry corpus: {declared} declared, {refused} refused under strict mode, 0 defaulted");
}
```

```rust
//! L4-01 at the boundary: the agent endpoint classifies by the decomposition registry, and under
//! strict mode an undeclared tool is refused before the proxy decides anything.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
use serde_json::Value;
use warrantor_warrant::effects::{Decomposition, DecompositionRegistry, UnclassifiedPolicy};

const NOW: u64 = 1_786_000_000;

fn now() -> u64 {
    NOW
}

fn tempdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let mut path = std::env::temp_dir();
    path.push(format!(
        "warrantor-effects-{tag}-{}-{}",
        std::process::id(),
        std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .expect("clock")
            .as_nanos()
    ));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&path).expect("tempdir");
    path
}

fn seed(dir: &Path, id: &str) -> StoredWarrant {
    let bounds = WarrantBounds {
        tools: ["files.write_file", "files.read_file"]
            .into_iter()
            .map(str::to_string)
            .collect(),
        write_paths: BTreeSet::new(),
        egress_hosts: BTreeSet::new(),
        staged_classes: [SideEffectClass::Write].into_iter().collect(),
        expires_at: NOW + 3600,
        budget_cents_observed: None,
        delegation_depth: 1,
    };
    let issuer = SigningKey::from_bytes(&[1; 32]);
    let settle = SigningKey::from_bytes(&[2; 32]);
    let warrant = Warrant::grant(
        id,
        "classify or refuse",
        "spiffe://muveraai.com/agent/a",
        bounds,
        NOW,
        &settle.verifying_key(),
        &issuer,
    )
    .expect("grant");
    let stored = StoredWarrant {
        warrant,
        worktree: None,
        repo: None,
        branch: None,
        base_commit: None,
        staged_chain: None,
    };
    WarrantStore::open(dir)
        .expect("store")
        .save(&stored)
        .expect("save");
    stored
}

fn path_argument() -> BTreeMap<String, Value> {
    // No dot, no scheme: the egress broker must find no destination in it, so the only thing
    // that can refuse these calls is the decomposition gate.
    let mut args = BTreeMap::new();
    args.insert("path".to_string(), Value::String("notes".to_string()));
    args
}

#[test]
fn strict_mode_refuses_an_undeclared_tool_before_the_proxy_and_names_it_afterwards() {
    let dir = tempdir("strict");
    let stored = seed(&dir, "wrt_strict");
    let store = WarrantStore::open(&dir).expect("store");
    let mut registry = DecompositionRegistry::builtin();
    registry
        .insert(Decomposition::parse("files.write_file=mutate").expect("parses"))
        .expect("insert");
    let mut endpoint =
        agent_endpoint_for(&stored, store.staged_path("wrt_strict"), ProxyMode::Enforce, now)
            .expect("endpoint")
            .with_decompositions(registry, UnclassifiedPolicy::Refuse);

    let refused = endpoint.call("files.read_file", &path_argument());
    assert!(refused.is_error);
    assert!(refused.text.contains("no declared effect decomposition"), "{}", refused.text);
    assert!(refused.text.contains("--upstream-effects 'files.read_file="), "{}", refused.text);

    // Declared: passes the gate, reaches the proxy, and is answered by the one honest thing a
    // session with no upstream can say. Not staged, because `EffectRegistry::github()` does not
    // know it -- that is Task 2.3's job, not this one's.
    let declared = endpoint.call("files.write_file", &path_argument());
    assert!(!declared.text.contains("no declared effect decomposition"), "{}", declared.text);
    assert!(declared.text.contains("no upstream MCP server is attached"), "{}", declared.text);

    assert_eq!(endpoint.unclassified_tools(), vec!["files.read_file".to_string()]);
}

#[test]
fn the_shipped_policy_still_guesses_and_still_names_the_guess() {
    let dir = tempdir("permissive");
    let stored = seed(&dir, "wrt_guess");
    let store = WarrantStore::open(&dir).expect("store");
    // No `with_decompositions` at all: the default is the builtin registry and GuessRead, which
    // is byte-for-byte what every session before this task did.
    let mut endpoint =
        agent_endpoint_for(&stored, store.staged_path("wrt_guess"), ProxyMode::Enforce, now)
            .expect("endpoint");
    let guessed = endpoint.call("files.read_file", &path_argument());
    assert!(!guessed.text.contains("no declared effect decomposition"), "{}", guessed.text);
    assert!(guessed.text.contains("no upstream MCP server is attached"), "{}", guessed.text);
    assert_eq!(endpoint.unclassified_tools(), vec!["files.read_file".to_string()]);
}
```

```rust
/// Build the session's decomposition registry: builtin, then every `--upstream-effects-file`,
/// then every `--upstream-effects '<tool>=<verb>+<verb>'`, refusing conflicts and the old flag.
///
/// `--upstream-class` is refused by name rather than ignored. An ignored flag would forward as a
/// read the very tool the operator typed the flag to protect, which is the guess this registry
/// exists to end.
///
/// # Errors
/// The first malformed value, unreadable file, foreign format, or conflicting declaration.
fn upstream_decompositions(args: &Args) -> Result<DecompositionRegistry, String> {
    if let Some(raw) = args.all("upstream-class").first() {
        return Err(format!(
            "--upstream-class is no longer read; got --upstream-class {raw:?}. Tools are declared \
             as effect syscalls now: --upstream-effects '<tool>=<verb>+<verb>' with verbs net, \
             cred, exec, mutate, msg, spend, delegate, actuate, attest -- a former 'write' is \
             usually 'mutate', a former 'destructive' is 'mutate+actuate', a former 'financial' \
             is 'spend'. Refusing rather than ignoring: an ignored flag would forward the tool it \
             named as a read."
        ));
    }
    let mut registry = DecompositionRegistry::builtin();
    for path in args.all("upstream-effects-file") {
        let body = std::fs::read_to_string(path)
            .map_err(|e| format!("--upstream-effects-file {path}: {e}"))?;
        let loaded = DecompositionRegistry::from_json(&body)
            .map_err(|e| format!("--upstream-effects-file {path}: {e}"))?;
        registry.merge(loaded)?;
    }
    for raw in args.all("upstream-effects") {
        let mut one = DecompositionRegistry::new();
        one.insert(Decomposition::parse(raw)?)?;
        registry.merge(one)?;
    }
    Ok(registry)
}

/// Strict mode: `--upstream-strict`, or its earlier spelling.
fn upstream_policy(args: &Args) -> UnclassifiedPolicy {
    if args.flags.contains_key("upstream-strict")
        || args.flags.contains_key("upstream-refuse-unclassified")
    {
        UnclassifiedPolicy::Refuse
    } else {
        UnclassifiedPolicy::GuessRead
    }
}
```
  (Merging a one-entry registry rather than calling `registry.insert` directly is what lets an operator restate a builtin identically on the command line without an error, while still refusing a different one.)

### Task 2.2: Signed tool and skill admission manifests (L4-09)

> **Anchor (plan-brief.md, L4-09):** "Every tool is signed, scoped and revocable before invocation, with provenance for the server that offers it: a signed manifest naming its effect decomposition (L4-01), its issuer, its version and its declared data classes. A tool server that cannot present a manifest is refused; a manifest whose decomposition disagrees with observed behavior is revoked. Guarantee class: chokepoint, bounded by the mediation ceiling." Verification gate: "An unsigned tool is refused; a signed tool whose runtime effects exceed its manifest is revoked within one invocation and the revocation is receipted; the admission decision itself verifies offline." Standards anchors S38 (MCP 2025-11-25 binds client credentials to the issuer that minted them) and S50 (the deployed authentication posture of remote MCP servers cannot be assumed).

**What exists today, exactly.** An upstream MCP server is attached by `crate::upstream::UpstreamSet::start(specs: &[UpstreamSpec], timeout: Duration) -> Result<Self, UpstreamError>` (`rust/warrant/src/upstream.rs:603`), which handshakes, reads `tools/list` once (`upstream.rs:382-415`) and refuses exactly one thing: a server publishing a lifecycle verb (`LIFECYCLE_VERBS`, `upstream.rs:88`). Nothing about the server is signed, pinned, versioned or classed, and `listChanged` is not consumed, so what the proxy knows about a server is what it published at attach. After Task 2.1, a tool's effects are whatever an operator declared through `crate::effects::DecompositionRegistry` (Task 2.1 Step 7) and, under `UnclassifiedPolicy::GuessRead`, an undeclared tool is still guessed `Read`. The only pinned trust on the machine is `crate::trust::Directory` (`trust.rs:63`, format `TRUST_FORMAT = "warrantor.trusted-issuers/1"`, `trust.rs:45`), mapping a name a human chose to an Ed25519 key checked out of band; it fetches nothing over a network (`trust.rs:18-22`). `rust/agent-manifest` (`warrantor_agent_manifest::SignedManifest`, `agent-manifest/src/lib.rs:127`) is a manifest for *agents*, not tools: its schema rejects unknown fields (`validate_object`, `lib.rs:153`), requires a `spiffe://` identity (`lib.rs:205`), carries the I-08 ladder `CAPABILITY_LADDER` (`lib.rs:30`) rather than the nine syscalls, and its `SignatureEnvelope.public_key` (`lib.rs:122`) embeds the verifying key *inside the signed file*, so `verify(sm)` (`lib.rs:526`) checks the file against a claim the file supplied. This task therefore does **not** consume `warrantor_agent_manifest`; it builds a tool manifest whose only trust input is a name resolved through the pinned directory (no new trust root), reusing that crate's canonical-JSON-then-sign *shape* and nothing of its types.

**Honest guarantee statement, written before the code.** The proxy observes two things about a tool server: what it *publishes* (`tools/list`, once, at attach) and what the agent *sends it* (call arguments, from which `crate::egress::destinations_of` extracts destinations, `egress.rs:354`). It cannot see what the server's process does on the network or the filesystem. "Runtime effects exceeding the manifest" therefore has two observable forms and one unobservable one, and this task names all three: (1) the server publishes a tool the manifest does not name, or a schema whose digest differs from the pinned one, which is attributable to the *server* itself, so the manifest is **revoked** and receipted before any call is forwarded; (2) a call to a tool whose manifest does not declare `Syscall::Net` names a destination, which is attributable to the *agent's* arguments, not the server, so the call is **refused** at an `admission` bound and receipted but the manifest is not revoked (an agent must not be able to revoke a tool by typing a URL into an argument); (3) a server with a compiled-in endpoint that never appears in an argument is invisible here, exactly as `egress.rs:338-340` already says of the egress bound. Every label in this task is `BoundStrength::Mediated` (`lib.rs:208`); nothing here is `Enforced`. The skill half of the item is weaker still and is labeled so: a skill file is loaded by the harness, never through the proxy (`harness::Coverage::McpAndBuiltins` sentence, `harness.rs:82-86`), so a skill manifest is admitted, receipted and checkable by digest, and `Observed` is the only honest tier for it.

**Sequencing.** This task branches from `main` *after* Task 2.1 has merged and consumes its symbols verbatim. A manifest is one more source of declarations for the registry Task 2.1 built: at attach, every admitted manifest is converted to a `DecompositionRegistry` and merged into the operator's, so classification stays on one path (`AgentEndpoint::with_decompositions`, Task 2.1 Step 11) and a manifest that disagrees with a `--upstream-effects` flag is a conflict refused at attach, never last-wins.

```rust
//! Signed tool and skill admission manifests (L4-09).
//!
//! A manifest is signed by the party that vouches for a tool server and is verified against a
//! key this machine pinned out of band under a NAME (`crate::trust`). No key travels inside the
//! file: a file that carries its own verifying key verifies nothing but its own consistency.
//! Everything decided here is decided at the MCP proxy and is `BoundStrength::Mediated`; the
//! skill half (`AdmissionKind::Skill`) has no chokepoint at all and is `Observed`.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use ed25519_dalek::{Signature, Signer, SigningKey, Verifier, VerifyingKey};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;
use thiserror::Error;

use crate::effects::{Decomposition, DecompositionRegistry, Syscall};
use crate::mcp::ToolSpec;
use crate::report::sha256_hex;
use crate::trust::Directory;

/// The manifest wire format. A new shape gets a new name, never a silent change.
pub const MANIFEST_FORMAT: &str = "warrantor.tool-manifest/1";
/// The admission receipt wire format.
pub const RECEIPT_FORMAT: &str = "warrantor.admission-receipt/1";
/// The export `warrantor verify` dispatches on.
pub const EXPORT_FORMAT: &str = "warrantor.admission-export/1";

const MANIFEST_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"warrantor-tool-manifest-v1";
const RECEIPT_DOMAIN: &[u8] = b"warrantor-admission-receipt-v1";

/// Length-prefixed, domain-separated signing input: the same shape `lib.rs` uses for warrants,
/// so a signature over one kind of object can never be replayed as another.
fn signing_input(domain: &[u8], body: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(domain.len() + body.len() + 16);
    out.extend_from_slice(&(domain.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(domain);
    out.extend_from_slice(&(body.len() as u64).to_le_bytes());
    out.extend_from_slice(body);
    out
}

/// What the manifest admits: an MCP tool server, or a skill file identified by content digest.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum AdmissionKind {
    /// An MCP server; `tools` names every tool it may publish.
    Tool,
    /// A skill file; `subject_digest` is its SHA-256 and `tools` names the tools it may call.
    Skill,
}

/// One tool's declared decomposition and data classes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ToolEntry {
    /// The syscalls this tool performs. Never empty: a tool with no effect still attests.
    pub effects: BTreeSet<Syscall>,
    /// Data classes the tool may receive or return, as the issuer names them. Recorded in the
    /// receipt; checked against a warrant bound only once Task 2.5 gives payloads a class.
    pub data_classes: BTreeSet<String>,
    /// SHA-256 hex of the tool's `inputSchema`, when pinned. A published schema that differs is
    /// the server's behavior disagreeing with its manifest.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub schema_digest: Option<String>,
}

/// The signed body.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ManifestClaims {
    /// Always [`MANIFEST_FORMAT`].
    pub format: String,
    /// The upstream name the tools are published under: the `UpstreamSpec::name` rule applies.
    pub server: String,
    /// Tool server or skill.
    pub kind: AdmissionKind,
    /// The issuer's version string. Recorded, not interpreted.
    pub version: String,
    /// The PINNED NAME of the signer in `trusted/issuers.json`. Never a key.
    pub issuer: String,
    /// Epoch seconds.
    pub issued_at: u64,
    /// Epoch seconds. A manifest without an end never ends, so zero is refused.
    pub expires_at: u64,
    /// For `Skill`: SHA-256 hex of the skill file. Refused when absent on a skill.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub subject_digest: Option<String>,
    /// Bare tool name (no `<server>.` prefix) -> entry. A `BTreeMap`, so the bytes are stable.
    pub tools: BTreeMap<String, ToolEntry>,
}

/// A manifest and its Ed25519 signature over `signing_input(MANIFEST_DOMAIN, canonical claims)`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SignedManifest {
    /// The claims.
    pub claims: ManifestClaims,
    /// Hex signature. Empty is "unsigned", and unsigned is refused by name.
    pub signature: String,
}

/// What refused, in one sentence the operator can act on.
#[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AdmissionError {
    /// The file's shape is wrong.
    #[error("manifest refused: {0}")]
    Format(String),
    /// The signature does not verify against the resolved issuer key.
    #[error("manifest refused: the signature does not verify against the pinned issuer key")]
    Signature,
    /// The manifest is past its end.
    #[error("manifest refused: it expired at {expires_at}; now is {now}")]
    Expired {
        /// Epoch seconds.
        expires_at: u64,
        /// Epoch seconds.
        now: u64,
    },
    /// The issuer name is not pinned on this machine.
    #[error("manifest refused: issuer {0:?} is not pinned on this machine. Check the issuer's key out of band and pin it: warrantor issuer add {0} <hex>")]
    UnpinnedIssuer(String),
    /// The file carries no signature at all.
    #[error("manifest refused: it is unsigned. A tool server that cannot present a signed manifest is refused, not guessed at")]
    Unsigned,
    /// The server publishes something its manifest does not name.
    #[error("server {server:?} revoked: {detail}")]
    Publication {
        /// The upstream name.
        server: String,
        /// What disagreed.
        detail: String,
    },
    /// The server's manifest was revoked earlier.
    #[error("server {server:?} was revoked at {at}: {reason}")]
    Revoked {
        /// The upstream name.
        server: String,
        /// Epoch seconds.
        at: u64,
        /// Why.
        reason: String,
    },
    /// The store could not be read or written.
    #[error("admission store: {0}")]
    Io(String),
}

fn canonical(claims: &ManifestClaims) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AdmissionError> {
    serde_json::to_vec(claims).map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Format(e.to_string()))
}
```

```rust
/// Sign claims with the issuer's key. The signature covers the canonical JSON of `claims`, which
/// is byte-stable because every map is a `BTreeMap` and the struct's field order is fixed.
#[must_use]
pub fn sign_manifest(claims: ManifestClaims, key: &SigningKey) -> SignedManifest {
    let body = canonical(&claims).expect("claims are always serializable");
    let signature = key.sign(&signing_input(MANIFEST_DOMAIN, &body));
    SignedManifest {
        claims,
        signature: hex::encode(signature.to_bytes()),
    }
}

/// Verify format, shape, signature and expiry against an issuer key the CALLER resolved.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`AdmissionError`] naming the first thing wrong. Shape is checked before the signature so a
/// file from a future build is refused for what it is rather than for a signature this build
/// cannot compute.
pub fn verify_manifest(
    manifest: &SignedManifest,
    issuer: &VerifyingKey,
    now: u64,
) -> Result<(), AdmissionError> {
    let claims = &manifest.claims;
    if claims.format != MANIFEST_FORMAT {
        return Err(AdmissionError::Format(format!(
            "it declares format {:?}, and this build reads only {MANIFEST_FORMAT}",
            claims.format
        )));
    }
    if claims.server.is_empty()
        || !claims
            .server
            .chars()
            .all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '-' || c == '_')
    {
        return Err(AdmissionError::Format(format!(
            "server {:?} must be letters, digits, '-' or '_', the same rule as --upstream",
            claims.server
        )));
    }
    crate::trust::check_name(&claims.issuer).map_err(AdmissionError::Format)?;
    if claims.expires_at == 0 {
        return Err(AdmissionError::Format(
            "expires_at is required: a manifest without an end never ends".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    if claims.kind == AdmissionKind::Skill && claims.subject_digest.is_none() {
        return Err(AdmissionError::Format(
            "a skill manifest must carry subject_digest, the SHA-256 of the skill file".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    if claims.tools.is_empty() {
        return Err(AdmissionError::Format(
            "a manifest naming no tools admits nothing; state the tools explicitly".to_string(),
        ));
    }
    for (tool, entry) in &claims.tools {
        if entry.effects.is_empty() {
            return Err(AdmissionError::Format(format!(
                "{tool} declares no effect syscall. A tool that only answers is `attest`; a \
                 tool with an effect must say which"
            )));
        }
    }
    if manifest.signature.is_empty() {
        return Err(AdmissionError::Unsigned);
    }
    let body = canonical(claims)?;
    let raw = hex::decode(&manifest.signature).map_err(|_| AdmissionError::Signature)?;
    let bytes: [u8; 64] = raw
        .as_slice()
        .try_into()
        .map_err(|_| AdmissionError::Signature)?;
    issuer
        .verify(
            &signing_input(MANIFEST_DOMAIN, &body),
            &Signature::from_bytes(&bytes),
        )
        .map_err(|_| AdmissionError::Signature)?;
    if now >= claims.expires_at {
        return Err(AdmissionError::Expired {
            expires_at: claims.expires_at,
            now,
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// SHA-256 hex over the serialized manifest, claims and signature: the identity every receipt
/// names, so a re-signed manifest is a different manifest.
#[must_use]
pub fn manifest_digest(manifest: &SignedManifest) -> String {
    let body = serde_json::to_vec(manifest).expect("a manifest is always serializable");
    sha256_hex(&body)
}
```

```rust
/// SHA-256 hex of a tool's `inputSchema`. `serde_json` in this workspace has no `preserve_order`,
/// so `Value::Object` is a `BTreeMap` and the bytes are key-sorted without a canonicalizer.
#[must_use]
pub fn schema_digest(schema: &Value) -> String {
    sha256_hex(&serde_json::to_vec(schema).expect("a Value is always serializable"))
}

/// Does what the server PUBLISHES agree with its manifest?
///
/// `published` carries `<server>.<tool>` names as [`crate::upstream::UpstreamSet::published_tools`]
/// returns them; other servers' tools are ignored. A tool not named, or a pinned schema whose
/// digest differs, is the server's own behavior disagreeing with its manifest.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`AdmissionError::Publication`] naming every disagreement, in name order.
pub fn check_publication(
    manifest: &SignedManifest,
    published: &[ToolSpec],
) -> Result<(), AdmissionError> {
    let server = &manifest.claims.server;
    let prefix = format!("{server}.");
    let mut faults = Vec::new();
    for tool in published {
        let Some(bare) = tool.name.strip_prefix(&prefix) else {
            continue;
        };
        match manifest.claims.tools.get(bare) {
            None => faults.push(format!("publishes {bare:?}, which the manifest does not name")),
            Some(entry) => {
                if let Some(pinned) = &entry.schema_digest {
                    let actual = schema_digest(&tool.input_schema);
                    if &actual != pinned {
                        faults.push(format!(
                            "publishes {bare:?} with schema {actual}, manifest pins {pinned}"
                        ));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if faults.is_empty() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    Err(AdmissionError::Publication {
        server: server.clone(),
        detail: faults.join("; "),
    })
}

/// The manifest as declarations for the effect registry, under `<server>.<tool>` names, so a
/// manifest classifies on the same path an operator's `--upstream-effects` does.
///
/// # Errors
/// The registry's own sentence for a tool that decomposes to nothing or is named twice; neither
/// is reachable for a manifest [`verify_manifest`] accepted.
pub fn decompositions_of(manifest: &SignedManifest) -> Result<DecompositionRegistry, String> {
    let mut registry = DecompositionRegistry::new();
    for (bare, entry) in &manifest.claims.tools {
        let published = format!("{}.{bare}", manifest.claims.server);
        registry.insert(Decomposition::new(&published, entry.effects.clone())?)?;
    }
    Ok(registry)
}
```

```rust
//! Admission: what is refused, what is receipted, and what a receipt proves offline.

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use ed25519_dalek::SigningKey;
use warrantor_warrant::admission::{
    manifest_digest, sign_manifest, verify_receipt, AdmissionDecision, AdmissionError,
    AdmissionKind, AdmittedSet, ManifestClaims, SignedManifest, ToolEntry, MANIFEST_FORMAT,
    RECEIPT_FORMAT,
};
use warrantor_warrant::effects::Syscall;
use warrantor_warrant::trust::Directory;

const NOW: u64 = 1_786_000_000;

fn key(byte: u8) -> SigningKey {
    SigningKey::from_bytes(&[byte; 32])
}

fn tempdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let mut path = std::env::temp_dir();
    path.push(format!(
        "warrantor-admission-{tag}-{}-{}",
        std::process::id(),
        std::time::SystemTime::now()
            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
            .map(|d| d.as_nanos())
            .unwrap_or(0)
    ));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&path).expect("tempdir");
    path
}

fn entry(effects: &[Syscall]) -> ToolEntry {
    ToolEntry {
        effects: effects.iter().copied().collect(),
        data_classes: ["public".to_string()].into_iter().collect(),
        schema_digest: None,
    }
}

/// The selftest server's manifest: `echo` with the effects given, `now` as a pure attestation.
fn selftest_manifest(echo_effects: &[Syscall]) -> ManifestClaims {
    let mut tools = BTreeMap::new();
    tools.insert("echo".to_string(), entry(echo_effects));
    tools.insert("now".to_string(), entry(&[Syscall::Attest]));
    ManifestClaims {
        format: MANIFEST_FORMAT.to_string(),
        server: "selftest".to_string(),
        kind: AdmissionKind::Tool,
        version: "1.0.0".to_string(),
        issuer: "vendor".to_string(),
        issued_at: NOW,
        expires_at: NOW + 86_400,
        subject_digest: None,
        tools,
    }
}

fn pinned(root: &Path, name: &str, vendor: &SigningKey) -> Directory {
    let mut directory = Directory::load(root).expect("empty");
    directory
        .pin(name, &vendor.verifying_key(), NOW, "test pin")
        .expect("pin");
    directory.save(root).expect("save");
    directory
}

#[test]
fn an_unsigned_manifest_is_refused_and_the_refusal_is_receipted() {
    let root = tempdir("unsigned");
    let vendor = key(7);
    let machine = key(1);
    let directory = pinned(&root, "vendor", &vendor);
    let unsigned = SignedManifest {
        claims: selftest_manifest(&[Syscall::Attest]),
        signature: String::new(),
    };
    let set = AdmittedSet::open(&root);
    let err = set
        .admit(&unsigned, &directory, &machine, NOW + 1)
        .expect_err("unsigned is refused");
    assert_eq!(err, AdmissionError::Unsigned);
    assert!(set.load("selftest").expect("read").is_none(), "nothing was admitted");
    let receipts = set.receipts().expect("ledger");
    assert_eq!(receipts.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(receipts[0].claims.decision, AdmissionDecision::Refused);
    assert_eq!(receipts[0].claims.format, RECEIPT_FORMAT);
    verify_receipt(&receipts[0], &machine.verifying_key()).expect("the refusal verifies");
}

#[test]
fn an_unpinned_issuer_is_refused_with_the_pin_command() {
    let root = tempdir("unpinned");
    let vendor = key(7);
    let signed = sign_manifest(selftest_manifest(&[Syscall::Attest]), &vendor);
    let directory = Directory::load(&root).expect("empty");
    let err = AdmittedSet::open(&root)
        .admit(&signed, &directory, &key(1), NOW + 1)
        .expect_err("nobody pinned vendor");
    assert_eq!(err, AdmissionError::UnpinnedIssuer("vendor".to_string()));
    assert!(err.to_string().contains("warrantor issuer add vendor"), "{err}");
}

#[test]
fn a_pinned_signed_manifest_is_admitted_receipted_and_revocable() {
    let root = tempdir("admit");
    let vendor = key(7);
    let machine = key(1);
    let directory = pinned(&root, "vendor", &vendor);
    let signed = sign_manifest(selftest_manifest(&[Syscall::Attest]), &vendor);
    let set = AdmittedSet::open(&root);

    let receipt = set.admit(&signed, &directory, &machine, NOW + 1).expect("admitted");
    assert_eq!(receipt.claims.decision, AdmissionDecision::Admitted);
    assert_eq!(receipt.claims.manifest_digest, manifest_digest(&signed));
    assert_eq!(receipt.claims.issuer_name, "vendor");
    assert_eq!(receipt.claims.issuer_key, hex::encode(vendor.verifying_key().to_bytes()));
    verify_receipt(&receipt, &machine.verifying_key()).expect("verifies");
    assert_eq!(
        verify_receipt(&receipt, &key(2).verifying_key()),
        Err(AdmissionError::Signature)
    );
    assert_eq!(set.load("selftest").expect("read"), Some(signed.clone()));

    let revoked = set
        .revoke("selftest", "operator: vendor advisory", &machine, NOW + 2)
        .expect("revoked");
    assert_eq!(revoked.claims.decision, AdmissionDecision::Revoked);
    assert_eq!(
        set.is_revoked("selftest").expect("read"),
        Some((NOW + 2, "operator: vendor advisory".to_string()))
    );
    assert!(set.load("selftest").expect("read").is_none(), "revoked is not loaded");
    assert!(
        matches!(
            set.admit(&signed, &directory, &machine, NOW + 3),
            Err(AdmissionError::Revoked { .. })
        ),
        "re-presenting the same manifest does not lift a revocation"
    );
    assert_eq!(set.receipts().expect("ledger").len(), 4);
}
```

```rust
/// What an admission receipt records having decided.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum AdmissionDecision {
    /// The manifest was verified and is now the authority for its server.
    Admitted,
    /// The manifest, or one call under it, was refused. The manifest's standing is unchanged.
    Refused,
    /// The manifest is withdrawn; its server is refused at attach until re-admitted by name.
    Revoked,
}

/// The signed body of a receipt.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ReceiptClaims {
    /// Always [`RECEIPT_FORMAT`].
    pub format: String,
    /// Epoch seconds.
    pub at: u64,
    /// The upstream name.
    pub server: String,
    /// [`manifest_digest`] of the manifest decided on; empty for a revocation of a server
    /// whose manifest is no longer loadable.
    pub manifest_digest: String,
    /// The decision.
    pub decision: AdmissionDecision,
    /// Why, in the operator's words or this module's sentence.
    pub reason: String,
    /// The pinned name the manifest's issuer resolved through; empty when it did not resolve.
    pub issuer_name: String,
    /// The hex key that name resolved to at the moment of decision; empty when it did not.
    pub issuer_key: String,
}

/// A receipt signed by THIS machine's issuer key, so a reader elsewhere can check who decided.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Receipt {
    /// The claims.
    pub claims: ReceiptClaims,
    /// Hex signature over `signing_input(RECEIPT_DOMAIN, canonical claims)`.
    pub signature: String,
    /// Hex verifying key of the signer, recorded for the reader. Verification takes the key
    /// from the caller, never from this field.
    pub signer_key: String,
}

/// Verify a receipt against the key the caller resolved.
///
/// # Errors
/// [`AdmissionError::Format`] on a foreign format, [`AdmissionError::Signature`] otherwise.
pub fn verify_receipt(receipt: &Receipt, signer: &VerifyingKey) -> Result<(), AdmissionError> {
    if receipt.claims.format != RECEIPT_FORMAT {
        return Err(AdmissionError::Format(format!(
            "receipt declares {:?}; this build reads {RECEIPT_FORMAT}",
            receipt.claims.format
        )));
    }
    let body =
        serde_json::to_vec(&receipt.claims).map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Format(e.to_string()))?;
    let raw = hex::decode(&receipt.signature).map_err(|_| AdmissionError::Signature)?;
    let bytes: [u8; 64] = raw
        .as_slice()
        .try_into()
        .map_err(|_| AdmissionError::Signature)?;
    signer
        .verify(
            &signing_input(RECEIPT_DOMAIN, &body),
            &Signature::from_bytes(&bytes),
        )
        .map_err(|_| AdmissionError::Signature)
}

/// `<root>/admitted/<server>.json`
#[must_use]
pub fn admitted_path(root: &Path, server: &str) -> PathBuf {
    root.join("admitted").join(format!("{server}.json"))
}

/// `<root>/admitted/<server>.revoked.json`
#[must_use]
pub fn revoked_path(root: &Path, server: &str) -> PathBuf {
    root.join("admitted").join(format!("{server}.revoked.json"))
}

/// `<root>/admission/ledger.jsonl`: one receipt per line, append-only, `sync_all` per line.
#[must_use]
pub fn ledger_path(root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    root.join("admission").join("ledger.jsonl")
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Revocation {
    at: u64,
    reason: String,
}

/// The manifests this store has admitted, and the ledger of every decision about them.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct AdmittedSet {
    root: PathBuf,
}

impl AdmittedSet {
    /// Open the set under a store root. Nothing is created until a decision is written.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn open(root: &Path) -> Self {
        Self {
            root: root.to_path_buf(),
        }
    }

    fn write_json(path: &Path, body: &[u8]) -> Result<(), AdmissionError> {
        if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Io(e.to_string()))?;
        }
        let temporary = path.with_extension("json.tmp");
        std::fs::write(&temporary, body).map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Io(e.to_string()))?;
        std::fs::rename(&temporary, path).map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Io(e.to_string()))
    }

    fn receipt(
        &self,
        claims: ReceiptClaims,
        signer: &SigningKey,
    ) -> Result<Receipt, AdmissionError> {
        let body =
            serde_json::to_vec(&claims).map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Format(e.to_string()))?;
        let signature = signer.sign(&signing_input(RECEIPT_DOMAIN, &body));
        let receipt = Receipt {
            claims,
            signature: hex::encode(signature.to_bytes()),
            signer_key: hex::encode(signer.verifying_key().to_bytes()),
        };
        let path = ledger_path(&self.root);
        if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Io(e.to_string()))?;
        }
        let line =
            serde_json::to_string(&receipt).map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Format(e.to_string()))?;
        use std::io::Write as _;
        let mut file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
            .create(true)
            .append(true)
            .open(&path)
            .map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Io(format!("open {}: {e}", path.display())))?;
        writeln!(file, "{line}").map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Io(e.to_string()))?;
        // Durable before the caller acts on the decision: a receipt still in a buffer when the
        // process dies is a decision nobody can later find.
        file.sync_all().map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Io(e.to_string()))?;
        Ok(receipt)
    }

    /// Whether a server is revoked, and since when.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`AdmissionError::Io`] when the revocation record exists and cannot be read.
    pub fn is_revoked(&self, server: &str) -> Result<Option<(u64, String)>, AdmissionError> {
        let path = revoked_path(&self.root, server);
        let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(&path) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let revocation: Revocation = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)
            .map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Io(format!("{} cannot be read: {e}", path.display())))?;
        Ok(Some((revocation.at, revocation.reason)))
    }

    /// The admitted manifest for a server, or `None` when none was admitted or it was revoked.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`AdmissionError::Io`] when a record exists and cannot be read.
    pub fn load(&self, server: &str) -> Result<Option<SignedManifest>, AdmissionError> {
        if self.is_revoked(server)?.is_some() {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let path = admitted_path(&self.root, server);
        let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(&path) else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        serde_json::from_slice(&bytes)
            .map(Some)
            .map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Io(format!("{} cannot be read: {e}", path.display())))
    }

    /// Verify a manifest against the pinned directory and, if it holds, make it the authority
    /// for its server. Every outcome, admitted or refused, is receipted before this returns.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// The refusal, after its receipt is durable.
    pub fn admit(
        &self,
        manifest: &SignedManifest,
        directory: &Directory,
        signer: &SigningKey,
        now: u64,
    ) -> Result<Receipt, AdmissionError> {
        let server = manifest.claims.server.clone();
        let issuer_name = manifest.claims.issuer.clone();
        let resolved = directory.resolve(&issuer_name);
        let issuer_key = resolved
            .map(|k| hex::encode(k.to_bytes()))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let outcome = match self.is_revoked(&server)? {
            Some((at, reason)) => Err(AdmissionError::Revoked {
                server: server.clone(),
                at,
                reason,
            }),
            None => match resolved {
                None => Err(AdmissionError::UnpinnedIssuer(issuer_name.clone())),
                Some(key) => verify_manifest(manifest, &key, now),
            },
        };
        let (decision, reason) = match &outcome {
            Ok(()) => (
                AdmissionDecision::Admitted,
                format!("issuer {issuer_name:?} pinned; signature verifies"),
            ),
            Err(e) => (AdmissionDecision::Refused, e.to_string()),
        };
        let receipt = self.receipt(
            ReceiptClaims {
                format: RECEIPT_FORMAT.to_string(),
                at: now,
                server: server.clone(),
                manifest_digest: manifest_digest(manifest),
                decision,
                reason,
                issuer_name,
                issuer_key,
            },
            signer,
        )?;
        outcome?;
        let body = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(manifest)
            .map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Format(e.to_string()))?;
        Self::write_json(&admitted_path(&self.root, &server), &body)?;
        Ok(receipt)
    }

    /// Withdraw a server's manifest. The admitted record stays on disk beside the revocation so
    /// a reader can see what was withdrawn; `load` returns `None` from here on.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`AdmissionError::Io`].
    pub fn revoke(
        &self,
        server: &str,
        reason: &str,
        signer: &SigningKey,
        now: u64,
    ) -> Result<Receipt, AdmissionError> {
        let digest = self
            .load(server)?
            .map(|m| manifest_digest(&m))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let revocation = Revocation {
            at: now,
            reason: reason.to_string(),
        };
        let body =
            serde_json::to_vec(&revocation).map_err(|e| AdmissionError::Format(e.to_string()))?;
        Self::write_json(&revoked_path(&self.root, server), &body)?;
        self.receipt(
            ReceiptClaims {
                format: RECEIPT_FORMAT.to_string(),
                at: now,
                server: server.to_string(),
                manifest_digest: digest,
                decision: AdmissionDecision::Revoked,
                reason: reason.to_string(),
                issuer_name: String::new(),
                issuer_key: String::new(),
            },
            signer,
        )
    }

    /// Receipt a call refused under an admitted manifest. The manifest's standing is unchanged:
    /// the refused thing was the AGENT's argument, not the server's behavior.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`AdmissionError::Io`].
    pub fn refuse_call(
        &self,
        server: &str,
        manifest: &SignedManifest,
        reason: &str,
        signer: &SigningKey,
        now: u64,
    ) -> Result<Receipt, AdmissionError> {
        self.receipt(
            ReceiptClaims {
                format: RECEIPT_FORMAT.to_string(),
                at: now,
                server: server.to_string(),
                manifest_digest: manifest_digest(manifest),
                decision: AdmissionDecision::Refused,
                reason: reason.to_string(),
                issuer_name: manifest.claims.issuer.clone(),
                issuer_key: String::new(),
            },
            signer,
        )
    }

    /// Every receipt in the ledger, in order. A line that will not parse refuses the whole read:
    /// a readable prefix of a ledger is what a truncation looks like.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    /// [`AdmissionError::Io`].
    pub fn receipts(&self) -> Result<Vec<Receipt>, AdmissionError> {
        let path = ledger_path(&self.root);
        let raw = match std::fs::read_to_string(&path) {
            Ok(raw) => raw,
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(Vec::new()),
            Err(e) => return Err(AdmissionError::Io(format!("read {}: {e}", path.display()))),
        };
        raw.lines()
            .filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty())
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(i, line)| {
                serde_json::from_str(line).map_err(|e| {
                    AdmissionError::Io(format!(
                        "{}: line {} will not parse: {e}",
                        path.display(),
                        i + 1
                    ))
                })
            })
            .collect()
    }
}
```

```rust
fn stored_open(id: &str, tools: &[&str], egress: &[&str]) -> StoredWarrant {
    let bounds = WarrantBounds {
        tools: tools.iter().map(|t| (*t).to_string()).collect(),
        write_paths: BTreeSet::new(),
        egress_hosts: egress.iter().map(|h| (*h).to_string()).collect(),
        staged_classes: [SideEffectClass::Write].into_iter().collect(),
        expires_at: NOW + 3600,
        budget_cents_observed: None,
        delegation_depth: 1,
    };
    let warrant = Warrant::grant(
        id,
        "admission",
        "spiffe://muveraai.com/agent/a",
        bounds,
        NOW,
        &key(2).verifying_key(),
        &key(1),
    )
    .expect("grant");
    StoredWarrant {
        warrant,
        worktree: None,
        repo: None,
        branch: None,
        base_commit: None,
        staged_chain: None,
    }
}

/// The binary under test as an upstream. Built directly, never parsed: a build directory may
/// contain spaces and `UpstreamSpec::parse` splits on whitespace.
fn selftest_spec() -> UpstreamSpec {
    UpstreamSpec {
        name: "selftest".to_string(),
        program: env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_warrantor").to_string(),
        args: vec!["selftest-upstream".to_string()],
    }
}

fn now() -> u64 {
    NOW + 10
}

fn text_arg(text: &str) -> BTreeMap<String, Value> {
    [("text".to_string(), json!(text))].into_iter().collect()
}

/// Admit `signed` and build a strict endpoint whose registry carries the manifest's declarations.
fn admitted_endpoint(
    root: &Path,
    signed: &SignedManifest,
    stored: &StoredWarrant,
) -> (AdmittedSet, warrantor_warrant::mcp_endpoints::AgentEndpoint) {
    let vendor = key(7);
    let machine = key(1);
    let directory = pinned(root, "vendor", &vendor);
    let set = AdmittedSet::open(root);
    set.admit(signed, &directory, &machine, NOW + 1).expect("admitted");
    let upstreams = UpstreamSet::start(&[selftest_spec()], Duration::from_secs(30)).expect("attach");
    let mut registry = DecompositionRegistry::builtin();
    registry
        .merge(decompositions_of(signed).expect("decomposes"))
        .expect("no conflict with the builtin four");
    let manifests: BTreeMap<String, SignedManifest> =
        [("selftest".to_string(), signed.clone())].into_iter().collect();
    let endpoint = agent_endpoint_for(stored, root.join("staged.jsonl"), ProxyMode::Enforce, now)
        .expect("endpoint")
        .with_upstreams(upstreams)
        .with_decompositions(registry, UnclassifiedPolicy::Refuse)
        .with_admission(set.clone(), manifests, machine);
    (set, endpoint)
}

#[test]
fn a_call_naming_a_destination_to_a_tool_whose_manifest_has_no_net_is_refused_and_receipted() {
    let root = tempdir("runtime");
    let signed = sign_manifest(selftest_manifest(&[Syscall::Attest]), &key(7));
    // The warrant ALLOWS example.com, so the egress bound is not what refuses this.
    let stored = stored_open("w-runtime", &["selftest.echo"], &["example.com"]);
    let (set, mut endpoint) = admitted_endpoint(&root, &signed, &stored);

    let result = endpoint.call("selftest.echo", &text_arg("see https://example.com/x"));
    assert!(result.is_error, "{}", result.text);
    assert!(result.text.contains("admission bound") && result.text.contains("net"), "{}", result.text);
    assert_eq!(endpoint.forwarding_counts(), Some((0, 0)), "nothing was forwarded");
    assert_eq!(endpoint.admission_refusals(), 1);

    let receipts = set.receipts().expect("ledger");
    let last = receipts.last().expect("a refusal receipt");
    assert_eq!(last.claims.decision, AdmissionDecision::Refused);
    assert!(last.claims.reason.contains("example.com"), "{}", last.claims.reason);
    verify_receipt(last, &key(1).verifying_key()).expect("the refusal verifies");
    assert!(
        set.load("selftest").expect("read").is_some(),
        "the manifest is NOT revoked by the agent's argument"
    );

    // A call within the manifest still works, so the check is a bound and not a kill.
    let ok = endpoint.call("selftest.echo", &text_arg("plain"));
    assert!(!ok.is_error, "{}", ok.text);
    assert_eq!(ok.text, "plain");
    assert_eq!(endpoint.forwarding_counts(), Some((1, 0)));
    assert!(endpoint.unclassified_tools().is_empty(), "the manifest declared every tool");
}

#[test]
fn a_tool_whose_manifest_declares_net_may_name_a_destination_the_warrant_allows() {
    let root = tempdir("net");
    let signed = sign_manifest(selftest_manifest(&[Syscall::Net]), &key(7));
    let stored = stored_open("w-net", &["selftest.echo"], &["example.com"]);
    let (_, mut endpoint) = admitted_endpoint(&root, &signed, &stored);
    let ok = endpoint.call("selftest.echo", &text_arg("see https://example.com/x"));
    assert!(!ok.is_error, "{}", ok.text);
    assert_eq!(endpoint.admission_refusals(), 0);
    // The warrant's egress bound still decides destinations the manifest permits.
    let refused = endpoint.call("selftest.echo", &text_arg("see https://other.example/x"));
    assert!(refused.is_error && refused.text.contains("egress_hosts"), "{}", refused.text);
}
```

```rust
    /// Attach admitted manifests. A builder for the same reason as [`Self::with_upstreams`]:
    /// what this machine has admitted is a property of the store, never of the signed warrant.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn with_admission(
        mut self,
        set: crate::admission::AdmittedSet,
        manifests: BTreeMap<String, crate::admission::SignedManifest>,
        signer: SigningKey,
    ) -> Self {
        self.admission = Some((set, manifests, signer));
        self
    }

    /// Calls refused at the admission bound this session.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn admission_refusals(&self) -> usize {
        self.admission_refusals
    }

    /// The admission refusal for a call, if its server was admitted and the manifest disclaims
    /// NET while the arguments name a destination. `None` is "no admission objection", which is
    /// also the answer for a server nobody admitted; that case is decided at attach, not here.
    fn admission_objection(&self, call: &ToolCall) -> Option<(String, crate::admission::SignedManifest, String)> {
        let (_, manifests, _) = self.admission.as_ref()?;
        let (server, bare) = call.tool.split_once('.')?;
        let manifest = manifests.get(server)?;
        let entry = manifest.claims.tools.get(bare)?;
        if entry.effects.contains(&crate::effects::Syscall::Net) {
            return None;
        }
        let first = crate::egress::destinations_of(call).into_iter().next()?;
        Some((
            server.to_string(),
            manifest.clone(),
            format!(
                "{} names destination {:?} in argument {:?}, and its admitted manifest declares \
                 no net effect",
                call.tool, first.host, first.argument
            ),
        ))
    }
```

```rust
/// Run the real binary against `root`, with the binary's own directory on PATH so an
/// `--upstream 'x=warrantor selftest-upstream'` value never has to carry a path with spaces.
fn warrantor(root: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> std::process::Output {
    let bin = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_warrantor"));
    let mut paths = vec![bin.parent().expect("a directory").to_path_buf()];
    if let Some(existing) = std::env::var_os("PATH") {
        paths.extend(std::env::split_paths(&existing));
    }
    let mut all: Vec<String> = args.iter().map(|a| (*a).to_string()).collect();
    all.push("--root".to_string());
    all.push(root.to_string_lossy().to_string());
    std::process::Command::new(&bin)
        .args(&all)
        .env("PATH", std::env::join_paths(paths).expect("joinable"))
        .output()
        .expect("run warrantor")
}

fn shown_hex(root: &Path) -> String {
    String::from_utf8_lossy(&warrantor(root, &["issuer", "show-hex"]).stdout)
        .lines()
        .find_map(|l| l.strip_prefix("issuer public key  ").map(str::trim).map(str::to_string))
        .expect("a key line")
}

fn machine_key(root: &Path) -> SigningKey {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(root.join("keys/issuer.key")).expect("the store's issuer key");
    SigningKey::from_bytes(&bytes.as_slice().try_into().expect("32 bytes"))
}

#[test]
fn the_cli_signs_admits_exports_verifies_offline_and_refuses_an_unadmitted_server() {
    let root = tempdir("cli");
    let vendor_root = tempdir("cli-vendor");
    // The vendor signs with its own store's issuer key; this machine pins that key by name.
    let claims_path = vendor_root.join("selftest.claims.json");
    std::fs::write(
        &claims_path,
        serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&selftest_manifest(&[Syscall::Attest])).expect("json"),
    )
    .expect("write claims");
    let manifest_path = vendor_root.join("selftest.manifest.json");
    let signed = warrantor(
        &vendor_root,
        &["tools", "sign", claims_path.to_str().expect("utf-8"), "--out", manifest_path.to_str().expect("utf-8")],
    );
    assert!(signed.status.success(), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&signed.stderr));
    let vendor_hex = shown_hex(&vendor_root);

    // Unpinned: refused, and the refusal is in the ledger.
    let refused = warrantor(&root, &["tools", "admit", manifest_path.to_str().expect("utf-8")]);
    assert!(!refused.status.success());
    assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&refused.stderr).contains("issuer add vendor"));
    assert_eq!(AdmittedSet::open(&root).receipts().expect("ledger").len(), 1);

    assert!(warrantor(&root, &["issuer", "add", "vendor", &vendor_hex]).status.success());
    let admitted = warrantor(&root, &["tools", "admit", manifest_path.to_str().expect("utf-8")]);
    assert!(admitted.status.success(), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&admitted.stderr));
    let listed = String::from_utf8_lossy(&warrantor(&root, &["tools", "list"]).stdout).to_string();
    assert!(listed.contains("admitted") && listed.contains("selftest"), "{listed}");

    // Export, then verify on a store that has pinned nothing, against the admitting key.
    let export = root.join("selftest.admission.json");
    assert!(warrantor(&root, &["tools", "export", "selftest", "--out", export.to_str().expect("utf-8")]).status.success());
    let machine_hex = shown_hex(&root);
    let clean = tempdir("cli-clean");
    let verdict = warrantor(&clean, &["verify", export.to_str().expect("utf-8"), "--issuer", &machine_hex]);
    assert!(verdict.status.success(), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&verdict.stderr));
    let out = String::from_utf8_lossy(&verdict.stdout);
    assert!(out.contains("VERIFIED") && out.contains("not checked against a pin on this machine"), "{out}");
    let no_anchor = warrantor(&clean, &["verify", export.to_str().expect("utf-8")]);
    assert!(!no_anchor.status.success(), "an export without an anchor verifies nothing");

    // A session under --require-admission refuses a server with no admitted manifest.
    let stored = stored_open("w-cli", &["other.echo"], &[]);
    warrantor_warrant::store::WarrantStore::open(&root).expect("store").create(&stored).expect("create");
    let refused = warrantor(
        &root,
        &["mcp", "--agent", "w-cli", "--require-admission", "--upstream", "other=warrantor selftest-upstream"],
    );
    assert!(!refused.status.success());
    let err = String::from_utf8_lossy(&refused.stderr);
    assert!(err.contains("no admitted manifest") && err.contains("tools admit"), "{err}");
}

fn a_server_publishing_beyond_its_manifest_is_revoked_at_attach_and_the_revocation_is_receipted() {
    let root = tempdir("attach");
    let vendor = key(7);
    // Names `echo` only; the selftest server also publishes `now`.
    let mut only_echo = selftest_manifest(&[Syscall::Attest]);
    only_echo.tools.remove("now");
    let signed = sign_manifest(only_echo, &vendor);
    let manifest_path = root.join("selftest.manifest.json");
    std::fs::write(&manifest_path, serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&signed).expect("json")).expect("write");
    let vendor_hex = hex::encode(vendor.verifying_key().to_bytes());
    assert!(warrantor(&root, &["issuer", "add", "vendor", &vendor_hex]).status.success());
    assert!(warrantor(&root, &["tools", "admit", manifest_path.to_str().expect("utf-8")]).status.success());

    let stored = stored_open("w-attach", &["selftest.echo"], &[]);
    warrantor_warrant::store::WarrantStore::open(&root).expect("store").create(&stored).expect("create");
    let session = warrantor(
        &root,
        &["mcp", "--agent", "w-attach", "--upstream", "selftest=warrantor selftest-upstream"],
    );
    assert!(!session.status.success(), "the session must not start");
    let err = String::from_utf8_lossy(&session.stderr);
    assert!(err.contains("revoked") && err.contains("\"now\""), "{err}");

    let set = AdmittedSet::open(&root);
    assert!(set.is_revoked("selftest").expect("read").is_some());
    let receipts = set.receipts().expect("ledger");
    let last = receipts.last().expect("the revocation");
    assert_eq!(last.claims.decision, AdmissionDecision::Revoked);
    assert!(last.claims.reason.contains("now"), "{}", last.claims.reason);
    verify_receipt(last, &machine_key(&root).verifying_key()).expect("the revocation verifies");

    // Revoked servers are refused at the next attach too, with or without --require-admission.
    let again = warrantor(
        &root,
        &["mcp", "--agent", "w-attach", "--upstream", "selftest=warrantor selftest-upstream"],
    );
    assert!(!again.status.success());
    assert!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&again.stderr).contains("was revoked at"));
}
```
